spec_text:
---- MODULE W4Od10m7p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Blocks, Orders, TopGen

VARIABLES guard, dropped, air, refused

vars == <<guard, dropped, air, refused>>

\* An outstanding drop order: the block it targets, its order number, and the
\* generation the dispatcher read off that block's guard register.
Tickets == [blk: Blocks, num: Orders, gen: 0..TopGen]

Outstanding(b) == {t \in air : t.blk = b}

TypeOK ==
    /\ guard \in [Blocks -> 0..TopGen]
    /\ dropped \subseteq Blocks
    /\ air \subseteq Tickets
    /\ refused \subseteq Orders

Init ==
    /\ guard = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]
    /\ dropped = {}
    /\ air = {}
    /\ refused = {}

\* The centre only writes orders for blocks that are still armed, and an order
\* number is reused only once its previous carrier has left the air interface.
Issue(b, n) ==
    /\ b \notin dropped
    /\ \A t \in air : t.num # n
    /\ air' = air \cup {[blk |-> b, num |-> n, gen |-> guard[b]]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<guard, dropped, refused>>

\* The compare-and-swap.  Bumping the register on success is what leaves every
\* other order already in the air one generation behind.
Execute(t) ==
    /\ t \in air
    /\ t.gen = guard[t.blk]
    /\ guard' = [guard EXCEPT ![t.blk] = @ + 1]
    /\ dropped' = dropped \cup {t.blk}
    /\ air' = air \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED refused

Refuse(t) ==
    /\ t \in air
    /\ t.gen # guard[t.blk]
    /\ refused' = refused \cup {t.num}
    /\ air' = air \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<guard, dropped>>

Lose(t) ==
    /\ t \in air
    /\ air' = air \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<guard, dropped, refused>>

\* Maintenance re-arms a block only once nothing for it is still in the air, so
\* wrapping its generation counter cannot resurrect an older order.
Rearm(b) ==
    /\ b \in dropped
    /\ Outstanding(b) = {}
    /\ dropped' = dropped \ {b}
    /\ guard' = [guard EXCEPT ![b] = IF @ = TopGen THEN 0 ELSE @ + 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<air, refused>>

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Blocks, n \in Orders : Issue(b, n)
    \/ \E t \in air : Execute(t)
    \/ \E t \in air : Refuse(t)
    \/ \E t \in air : Lose(t)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : Rearm(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Nothing still in the air for an already-dropped block can compare equal to
\* that block's register, which is why the irreversible drop cannot land twice.
StaleAfterDrop ==
    \A t \in air : t.blk \in dropped => t.gen # guard[t.blk]

====
nl:
A subway signalling centre protects each track block with an emergency brake drop. Dropping the
brake on a block is irreversible from the software's point of view: once the shoe is released onto
the rail only a maintenance crew walking the tunnel can lift it again, so the signalling logic must
never land a second drop on a block that is already down, even when two dispatchers react to the
same hazard at once.

Each block carries a compare-and-swap guard register holding a generation number. A dispatcher who
wants to drop a block reads that block's current generation and stamps it onto a drop order, which
goes out over the trackside radio. The air interface is not ordered: orders sit on it and are picked
up in any sequence, so an order written first may well be acted on last.

The receiver acts on an order only if the generation stamped on it still equals the block's guard
register. On a match the brake drops, the block is recorded as down, and the register is bumped, so
every other order for that block already on the air is now one generation behind and can never
compare equal again. On a mismatch the receiver throws the order away and files its number on a
refused list. The radio link can also simply swallow an order without filing it anywhere.

The centre writes orders only for blocks that are still armed, and it reuses an order number only
once the previous order bearing that number has left the air interface, so two live orders never
share a number. When maintenance re-arms a dropped block they first confirm nothing for that block
is still outstanding on the air, and only then lift the shoe and roll the guard register on to its
next generation, wrapping back to zero at the top of the range.

The full set of actions is: Issue, in which the centre picks an armed block and a free order number,
reads the block's guard register and puts a stamped drop order on the air; Execute, in which the
receiver takes an order whose stamp equals the guard register, drops that block's brake, marks the
block down and bumps the register; Refuse, in which the receiver takes an order whose stamp no
longer equals the register and moves its number to the refused list; Lose, in which the air
interface swallows any outstanding order without a trace; and Rearm, in which maintenance lifts a
dropped block that has nothing outstanding on the air and rolls its guard register forward, wrapping
at the top.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every drop order still sitting on the air interface for a block whose brake is
already down carries a generation different from that block's guard register, so no outstanding
order can ever land a second brake drop on an already-dropped block.

---- MODULE W4Od6m2p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cars, Floors, NoCar

VARIABLES phase, cand, ballot, ledger, riser, staffed

vars == <<phase, cand, ballot, ledger, riser, staffed>>

Slots == Cars \cup {NoCar}

TypeOK ==
    /\ phase \in {"idle", "voting"}
    /\ cand \in Slots
    /\ ballot \in [Floors -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]
    /\ ledger \in [Floors -> Slots]
    /\ riser \subseteq Cars
    /\ staffed \subseteq Floors

Occupant == IF riser = {} THEN NoCar ELSE CHOOSE c \in riser : TRUE

Init ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ cand = NoCar
    /\ ballot = [f \in Floors |-> "none"]
    /\ ledger = [f \in Floors |-> NoCar]
    /\ riser = {}
    /\ staffed = Floors

Propose(c) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ cand' = c
    /\ phase' = "voting"
    /\ ballot' = [f \in Floors |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ledger, riser, staffed>>

\* A staffed floor votes yes only when its own ledger shows the express riser
\* unclaimed; that local check is the whole of the exclusion argument.
VoteYes(f) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ f \in staffed
    /\ ballot[f] = "none"
    /\ ledger[f] = NoCar
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![f] = "yes"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, cand, ledger, riser, staffed>>

VoteNo(f) ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ f \in staffed
    /\ ballot[f] = "none"
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![f] = "no"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, cand, ledger, riser, staffed>>

Commit ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \A f \in staffed : ballot[f] = "yes"
    /\ ledger' = [f \in Floors |-> IF f \in staffed THEN cand ELSE ledger[f]]
    /\ riser' = riser \cup {cand}
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ cand' = NoCar
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, staffed>>

Abort ==
    /\ phase = "voting"
    /\ \E f \in staffed : ballot[f] = "no"
    /\ phase' = "idle"
    /\ cand' = NoCar
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ballot, ledger, riser, staffed>>

Release(c) ==
    /\ c \in riser
    /\ riser' = riser \ {c}
    /\ ledger' = [f \in Floors |-> IF f \in staffed THEN NoCar ELSE ledger[f]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, cand, ballot, staffed>>

\* The staffed set is the running capacity: desks close and reopen between
\* rounds, and a reopening desk resyncs its ledger before it may vote again.
CloseDesk(f) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ f \in staffed
    /\ staffed \ {f} # {}
    /\ staffed' = staffed \ {f}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, cand, ballot, ledger, riser>>

OpenDesk(f) ==
    /\ phase = "idle"
    /\ f \notin staffed
    /\ staffed' = staffed \cup {f}
    /\ ledger' = [ledger EXCEPT ![f] = Occupant]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<phase, cand, ballot, riser>>

Balloting == \E f \in Floors : VoteYes(f) \/ VoteNo(f)

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Propose(c)
    \/ Balloting
    \/ Commit \/ Abort
    \/ \E c \in Cars : Release(c)
    \/ \E f \in Floors : CloseDesk(f) \/ OpenDesk(f)

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Balloting) /\ WF_vars(Commit) /\ WF_vars(Abort)

\* Every staffed floor's ledger names whoever is in the riser, so a second car
\* can never collect a unanimous yes while the first is still up there.
LedgerNamesOccupant ==
    \A c \in riser : \A f \in staffed : ledger[f] = c

\* Fairness of balloting and of the coordinator's decision drains every round.
RoundsResolve == (phase = "voting") ~> (phase = "idle")

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cars = {carA, carB}
    Floors = {fLobby, fSky}
    NoCar = NoCar
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT LedgerNamesOccupant
PROPERTY RoundsResolve
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper has one express riser that a car can be lifted into for a
non-stop run. Only one car may be up the riser at a time, and the bank has no central arbiter it
trusts: the decision is taken by two-phase commit across the floor desks that are currently staffed.

A round begins when the dispatcher proposes a car. Every staffed desk then casts one ballot. A desk
votes yes only when its own ledger shows the riser unclaimed; if its ledger already names a car, or
if the desk simply does not like the request, it votes no. When every staffed desk has voted yes the
coordinator commits: each staffed desk writes the candidate into its ledger and the car is lifted
into the riser. If any staffed desk voted no, the round aborts and nothing is written. Either way
the round ends and the dispatcher is free to propose again.

A car that has finished its run is released: it leaves the riser and every staffed desk clears its
ledger entry.

The staffing level changes at runtime. Between rounds a desk can be closed, shrinking the set of
voters the coordinator needs unanimity from, as long as at least one desk stays open. A closed desk
can reopen, again only between rounds, and when it does it resyncs its ledger from the bank so that
it comes back knowing who, if anyone, is up the riser. Desks never open or close mid-ballot, so the
voter set is fixed for the length of a round.

The full set of actions is: Propose, in which the dispatcher names a candidate car and opens a
ballot; VoteYes, in which a staffed desk with an unclaimed ledger votes in favour; VoteNo, in which a
staffed desk votes against; Commit, in which unanimous yes votes write the candidate into every
staffed desk's ledger and lift it into the riser; Abort, in which a single no vote ends the round
with nothing written; Release, in which a car leaves the riser and the staffed desks clear their
ledgers; CloseDesk, in which a desk shuts between rounds while at least one other stays open; and
OpenDesk, in which a closed desk reopens between rounds and resyncs its ledger from the bank.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a car is up the express riser, every staffed desk's ledger names that car,
so no second car can ever assemble the unanimous yes vote it would need to be lifted.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every ballot that opens is eventually resolved, so the bank always returns to a
state in which the dispatcher can propose again.

---- MODULE W4Od15m1p2t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS RingSize, Tags, TotalLots, MaxQty

Desks == 0 .. RingSize - 1
Nxt(d) == (d + 1) % RingSize

VARIABLES book, wire, baton, torn

vars == <<book, wire, baton, torn>>

\* A consignment on the wire.  The tag makes two otherwise identical
\* consignments distinct, so the wire cannot silently coalesce them.
Notes == [tag: Tags, src: Desks, dst: Desks, qty: 1 .. MaxQty]

RECURSIVE Held(_)
Held(S) == IF S = {} THEN 0
           ELSE LET d == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN book[d] + Held(S \ {d})

RECURSIVE Afloat(_)
Afloat(W) == IF W = {} THEN 0
             ELSE LET n == CHOOSE x \in W : TRUE IN n.qty + Afloat(W \ {n})

TypeOK ==
    /\ book \in [Desks -> 0 .. TotalLots]
    /\ wire \subseteq Notes
    /\ baton \in Desks
    /\ torn \subseteq Tags

Free(t) == \A n \in wire : n.tag # t

Init ==
    /\ book = [d \in Desks |-> IF d = 0 THEN TotalLots ELSE 0]
    /\ wire = {}
    /\ baton = 0
    /\ torn = {}

\* The baton walks the ring; only the desk holding it may release lots.
PassBaton ==
    /\ baton' = Nxt(baton)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, wire, torn>>

Consign(d, t, q) ==
    /\ baton = d
    /\ Free(t)
    /\ q <= book[d]
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![d] = @ - q]
    /\ wire' = wire \cup {[tag |-> t, src |-> d, dst |-> Nxt(d), qty |-> q]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, torn>>

\* Consignments are picked off the wire in any order, not the order they were
\* released, so an older note may settle long after a newer one.
Settle(n) ==
    /\ n \in wire
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![n.dst] = @ + n.qty]
    /\ wire' = wire \ {n}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, torn>>

Recall(n) ==
    /\ n \in wire
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![n.src] = @ + n.qty]
    /\ wire' = wire \ {n}
    /\ torn' = torn \cup {n.tag}
    /\ UNCHANGED baton

Next ==
    \/ PassBaton
    \/ \E d \in Desks, t \in Tags, q \in 1 .. MaxQty : Consign(d, t, q)
    \/ \E n \in wire : Settle(n)
    \/ \E n \in wire : Recall(n)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Lots are only ever moved between a desk and the wire, never minted or burnt,
\* so the exchange-wide total is fixed for the whole session.
LotsConserved == Held(Desks) + Afloat(wire) = TotalLots

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    RingSize = 3
    Tags = {tg1, tg2}
    TotalLots = 2
    MaxQty = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT LotsConserved
nl:
A stock exchange runs its opening auction across a ring of member desks. The whole session starts
with a fixed pool of share lots sitting on the first desk, and the auction only ever moves lots
around the ring; the exchange never mints a lot and never destroys one, so at any instant the lots
sitting on desks plus the lots still travelling must add up to the pool the session opened with.

The right to release lots travels with a baton that walks the ring one desk at a time. A desk may
release lots only while it is holding the baton, and it releases them by writing a consignment note
addressed to the next desk round the ring: the note carries a quantity, which is deducted from the
releasing desk's holdings at the moment the note is written. Notes carry a tag drawn from a small
pool, and a tag is reused only when no note bearing it is still in flight, so two notes on the wire
are always distinguishable.

The settlement wire does not preserve order. Notes sit on it and are picked off in whatever sequence
the settlement system gets to them, so a note written early may be credited long after one written
later. When a note is picked off normally, its quantity is credited to the desk it was addressed to.
A note can instead be torn up, in which case the quantity goes back to the desk that released it and
the tag is recorded on the torn list. Either way the quantity leaves the wire exactly as it arrived.

The full set of actions is: PassBaton, in which the baton moves to the next desk round the ring;
Consign, in which the desk holding the baton deducts a quantity from its own holdings and puts a
freshly tagged note for the next desk onto the settlement wire; Settle, in which any note on the
wire, in any order, is credited to the desk it was addressed to and leaves the wire; and Recall, in
which any note on the wire is torn up, its quantity credited back to the desk that released it and
its tag filed on the torn list.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The lots held across all desks plus the quantities on all notes still travelling on
the settlement wire always equal the total the session opened with.

---- MODULE W4Od16m8p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Techs, Drawers, MaxEpoch, NoTech

VARIABLES bayHeld, drwHeld, badge, roster, rosterEpoch

vars == <<bayHeld, drwHeld, badge, roster, rosterEpoch>>

Hands == Techs \cup {NoTech}

TypeOK ==
    /\ bayHeld \in Hands
    /\ drwHeld \in [Drawers -> Hands]
    /\ badge \in [Techs -> 0 .. MaxEpoch]
    /\ roster \subseteq Techs
    /\ rosterEpoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch

Current(t) == t \in roster /\ badge[t] = rosterEpoch

Init ==
    /\ bayHeld = NoTech
    /\ drwHeld = [d \in Drawers |-> NoTech]
    /\ badge = [t \in Techs |-> 0]
    /\ roster = Techs
    /\ rosterEpoch = 0

\* Coarse before fine: the bay interlock admits one technician at a time, and
\* only whoever is inside the bay may take a drawer, one drawer at a time.
EnterBay(t) ==
    /\ Current(t)
    /\ bayHeld = NoTech
    /\ bayHeld' = t
    /\ UNCHANGED <<drwHeld, badge, roster, rosterEpoch>>

TakeDrawer(t, d) ==
    /\ Current(t)
    /\ bayHeld = t
    /\ drwHeld[d] = NoTech
    /\ \A k \in Drawers : drwHeld[k] # t
    /\ drwHeld' = [drwHeld EXCEPT ![d] = t]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bayHeld, badge, roster, rosterEpoch>>

Dispense(t, d) ==
    /\ drwHeld[d] = t
    /\ Current(t)
    /\ drwHeld' = [drwHeld EXCEPT ![d] = NoTech]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bayHeld, badge, roster, rosterEpoch>>

LeaveBay(t) ==
    /\ bayHeld = t
    /\ \A d \in Drawers : drwHeld[d] # t
    /\ bayHeld' = NoTech
    /\ UNCHANGED <<drwHeld, badge, roster, rosterEpoch>>

\* The pharmacist-in-charge may turn the roster epoch at any moment; every
\* badge is stale from that instant, so the turn also strips every interlock.
RotateEpoch ==
    /\ rosterEpoch < MaxEpoch
    /\ rosterEpoch' = rosterEpoch + 1
    /\ bayHeld' = NoTech
    /\ drwHeld' = [d \in Drawers |-> NoTech]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<badge, roster>>

Rebadge(t) ==
    /\ t \in roster
    /\ badge[t] # rosterEpoch
    /\ badge' = [badge EXCEPT ![t] = rosterEpoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bayHeld, drwHeld, roster, rosterEpoch>>

\* Privileged override: a technician is struck off mid-shift and whatever they
\* are holding is broken open on the spot.
StrikeOff(t) ==
    /\ t \in roster
    /\ roster' = roster \ {t}
    /\ bayHeld' = IF bayHeld = t THEN NoTech ELSE bayHeld
    /\ drwHeld' = [d \in Drawers |-> IF drwHeld[d] = t THEN NoTech ELSE drwHeld[d]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<badge, rosterEpoch>>

Reinstate(t) ==
    /\ t \notin roster
    /\ roster' = roster \cup {t}
    /\ badge' = [badge EXCEPT ![t] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bayHeld, drwHeld, rosterEpoch>>

Serving == \E t \in Techs, d \in Drawers : Dispense(t, d)

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Techs : EnterBay(t) \/ LeaveBay(t) \/ Rebadge(t)
    \/ \E t \in Techs, d \in Drawers : TakeDrawer(t, d)
    \/ Serving
    \/ RotateEpoch
    \/ \E t \in Techs : StrikeOff(t) \/ Reinstate(t)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Serving)

\* Nobody struck off the roster and nobody carrying a superseded badge is ever
\* found holding a drawer open.
NoStaleHandInDrawer ==
    \A d \in Drawers :
        drwHeld[d] # NoTech => (drwHeld[d] \in roster /\ badge[drwHeld[d]] = rosterEpoch)

\* Because the bay admits one technician holding one drawer, fair dispensing
\* closes whichever drawer is open.
DrawersClose ==
    \A d \in Drawers : (drwHeld[d] # NoTech) ~> (drwHeld[d] = NoTech)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Techs = {tAnn, tBo}
    Drawers = {dwOpioid, dwSedative, dwFridge}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    NoTech = NoTech
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoStaleHandInDrawer
PROPERTY DrawersClose
nl:
A hospital pharmacy keeps its controlled drugs in a secure dispensing bay whose individual drawers
are separately latched. Access is hierarchical: the bay interlock is coarse and admits one
technician at a time, and only the technician who is inside the bay may take the fine interlock on a
drawer, one drawer at a time. The bay can only be given back once that technician is holding no
drawer.

Authorisation is by badge. The pharmacist-in-charge keeps a roster of technicians on shift together
with a roster epoch, and a technician may act only while they are on the roster and their badge
carries the current epoch. Turning the epoch is how the pharmacist invalidates every badge at once
at a shift change; because every badge is stale from that instant, the turn also strips the bay
interlock and every drawer latch. A technician still on the roster can re-badge to the current epoch
and carry on.

The pharmacist also has a privileged override aimed at individuals: a technician can be struck off
the roster mid-shift, and whatever they are holding is broken open on the spot rather than waiting
for them to hand it back. Somebody struck off can be reinstated later, but they return with a zeroed
badge and must re-badge before they can act again.

The full set of actions is: EnterBay, in which a currently authorised technician takes the free bay
interlock; TakeDrawer, in which the authorised technician inside the bay takes a free drawer latch
while holding no other drawer; Dispense, in which that technician hands out the medication and
latches the drawer shut again; LeaveBay, in which a technician holding no drawer gives the bay
interlock back; RotateEpoch, in which the pharmacist turns the roster epoch and the bay interlock
and every drawer latch are stripped; Rebadge, in which a rostered technician refreshes a stale badge
to the current epoch; StrikeOff, in which the pharmacist removes a technician from the roster and
breaks open whatever they are holding; and Reinstate, in which a struck-off technician is put back
on the roster with a zeroed badge.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any technician found holding a drawer open is on the current roster and carries a
badge stamped with the current roster epoch, so no struck-off or stale hand is ever inside a drawer.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every drawer that is opened is eventually latched shut again.

---- MODULE W4Od6m5p1t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Ctrls, Plans, MaxRev, Blank, NoBid

VARIABLES journal, bid, seenRev, seenPlan

vars == <<journal, bid, seenRev, seenPlan>>

Quorums == {q \in SUBSET Ctrls : 2 * Cardinality(q) > Cardinality(Ctrls)}

Bids == [base: 0 .. MaxRev, plan: Plans, yes: SUBSET Ctrls]

TypeOK ==
    /\ journal \in Seq(Plans)
    /\ bid \in Bids \cup {NoBid}
    /\ seenRev \in [Ctrls -> 0 .. MaxRev]
    /\ seenPlan \in [Ctrls -> Plans \cup {Blank}]

Init ==
    /\ journal = <<>>
    /\ bid = NoBid
    /\ seenRev = [c \in Ctrls |-> 0]
    /\ seenPlan = [c \in Ctrls |-> Blank]

\* A controller may only put up a revision of the plan it has actually read, so
\* every bid carries the revision number it was derived from.
Propose(c, p) ==
    /\ bid = NoBid
    /\ bid' = [base |-> seenRev[c], plan |-> p, yes |-> {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, seenRev, seenPlan>>

\* A controller votes for a bid only if the bid was derived from exactly the
\* revision that controller itself has in front of it.
Vote(c) ==
    /\ bid # NoBid
    /\ c \notin bid.yes
    /\ bid.base = seenRev[c]
    /\ bid' = [bid EXCEPT !.yes = @ \cup {c}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, seenRev, seenPlan>>

Commit ==
    /\ bid # NoBid
    /\ bid.yes \in Quorums
    /\ bid.base = Len(journal)
    /\ Len(journal) < MaxRev
    /\ journal' = Append(journal, bid.plan)
    /\ bid' = NoBid
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seenRev, seenPlan>>

Discard ==
    /\ bid # NoBid
    /\ bid' = NoBid
    /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, seenRev, seenPlan>>

Sync(c) ==
    /\ seenRev' = [seenRev EXCEPT ![c] = Len(journal)]
    /\ seenPlan' = [seenPlan EXCEPT ![c] =
                        IF journal = <<>> THEN Blank ELSE journal[Len(journal)]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<journal, bid>>

\* Privileged override: the chief engineer writes the bank plan directly and
\* every controller's copy is left behind at whatever revision it had read.
Override(p) ==
    /\ Len(journal) < MaxRev
    /\ journal' = Append(journal, p)
    /\ bid' = NoBid
    /\ UNCHANGED <<seenRev, seenPlan>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls, p \in Plans : Propose(c, p)
    \/ \E c \in Ctrls : Vote(c) \/ Sync(c)
    \/ Commit \/ Discard
    \/ \E p \in Plans : Override(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No controller ever holds a plan that is not the committed plan at the very
\* revision it believes it is on, so a write can never be silently overwritten
\* underneath a controller that thinks it is up to date.
MirrorMatchesJournal ==
    \A c \in Ctrls :
        seenRev[c] > 0 => (seenRev[c] <= Len(journal) /\ seenPlan[c] = journal[seenRev[c]])

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Ctrls = {cNorth, cSouth, cWest}
    Plans = {pExpress, pLocal}
    MaxRev = 2
    Blank = Blank
    NoBid = NoBid
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT MirrorMatchesJournal
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper is driven by a shared dispatch plan that says which cars serve
which floor groups. Three floor controllers each keep their own copy of the plan, and the plan
itself lives in a revision journal: revision one is the first plan ever committed, revision two the
next, and so on. The danger the bank has to rule out is a lost update, where one controller's
revision is quietly written over while another controller still believes its own copy is current.

A change is made by quorum vote. A controller puts up a bid: the new plan it wants, stamped with the
revision number of the copy it actually has in front of it. Other controllers vote on that bid, and
a controller votes for it only when the bid was derived from exactly the revision that controller
itself is holding — a bid built on an older revision than what a voter has read gets no vote from
that voter. Once a strict majority of controllers has voted for the bid, and the bid's base revision
is still the newest revision in the journal, it commits and becomes the next journal entry. A bid
can also simply be withdrawn, and only one bid is ever on the table at a time.

A controller refreshes its copy by syncing: it takes the newest journal entry and the revision
number that goes with it. Until it does, it keeps the older copy it read, and it keeps voting on the
basis of that older revision.

The chief engineer has a privileged override and can append a plan to the journal directly, with no
bid and no vote. Any bid on the table is dropped, and every controller is left holding whatever
revision it last read.

The full set of actions is: Propose, in which a controller puts up a bid stamped with the revision
it currently holds; Vote, in which a controller adds its vote to a bid whose base revision matches
the one it is holding; Commit, in which a bid with a majority and a base equal to the newest journal
revision is appended to the journal; Discard, in which the bid on the table is withdrawn; Sync, in
which a controller refreshes its copy and revision number from the newest journal entry; and
Override, in which the chief engineer appends a plan to the journal directly and drops any bid.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every controller that holds a revision at all holds exactly the plan the journal
records at that revision number, so no committed plan is ever silently replaced underneath a
controller that believes it is current.

EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Ctrls, Cars, Landings, MaxTerm, NoCall, Idle

VARIABLES hall, backers, term, stamp, serving

vars == <<hall, backers, term, stamp, serving>>

Quorums == {q \in SUBSET Ctrls : 2 * Cardinality(q) > Cardinality(Ctrls)}

TypeOK ==
    /\ hall \in Landings \cup {NoCall}
    /\ backers \subseteq Ctrls
    /\ term \in 0 .. MaxTerm
    /\ stamp \in [Ctrls -> 0 .. MaxTerm]
    /\ serving \in Cars \cup {Idle}

Init ==
    /\ hall = NoCall
    /\ backers = {}
    /\ term = 0
    /\ stamp = [c \in Ctrls |-> 0]
    /\ serving = Idle

Press(f) ==
    /\ hall = NoCall
    /\ hall' = f
    /\ backers' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, stamp, serving>>

\* A controller may back the live call only while its own stamp matches the
\* running term; that check is the whole of the eligibility rule.
Back(c) ==
    /\ hall # NoCall
    /\ stamp[c] = term
    /\ c \notin backers
    /\ backers' = backers \cup {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hall, term, stamp, serving>>

Dispatch(k) ==
    /\ hall # NoCall
    /\ serving = Idle
    /\ backers \in Quorums
    /\ serving' = k
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hall, backers, term, stamp>>

Arrive ==
    /\ serving # Idle
    /\ hall' = NoCall
    /\ backers' = {}
    /\ serving' = Idle
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, stamp>>

\* An emergency re-election happens between dispatches: the term advances and
\* every backing collected under the old term is torn up rather than carried on.
Reelect ==
    /\ serving = Idle
    /\ term < MaxTerm
    /\ term' = term + 1
    /\ backers' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hall, stamp, serving>>

Restamp ==
    /\ \E c \in Ctrls : stamp[c] # term
    /\ stamp' = [c \in Ctrls |-> term]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hall, backers, term, serving>>

\* Privileged override: the building engineer kills a live call outright, car
\* and backings included, without waiting for anyone to agree.
Override ==
    /\ hall # NoCall
    /\ hall' = NoCall
    /\ backers' = {}
    /\ serving' = Idle
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, stamp>>

Backing == \E c \in Ctrls : Back(c)
Moving == \E k \in Cars : Dispatch(k)

Next ==
    \/ \E f \in Landings : Press(f)
    \/ Backing \/ Moving \/ Arrive \/ Reelect \/ Restamp \/ Override

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Backing) /\ WF_vars(Restamp) /\ WF_vars(Moving) /\ WF_vars(Arrive)

\* A car is only ever on its way under a majority every one of whose members
\* still carries the running term stamp.
WarrantedDispatch ==
    (serving # Idle) =>
        /\ backers \in Quorums
        /\ \A c \in backers : stamp[c] = term

\* Every landing call is eventually answered or killed.
CallsAnswered == (hall # NoCall) ~> (hall = NoCall)

====
nl:
An elevator bank in a skyscraper answers landing calls by a vote of its control panel rather than by
a single dispatcher. Three controllers sit on the panel and every dispatch needs a strict majority of
them behind it. The bank runs in terms: each controller carries a term stamp, and the building's
safety case says a controller whose stamp is behind the running term must not count towards any
decision, because it is reasoning from a picture of the bank that has since been replaced.

A landing call is pressed on one of the landings and stays live until it is answered. While the call
is live, controllers back it one at a time, and a controller may back it only while its stamp
matches the running term. Once a majority is behind the call and no car is already on its way, a car
is sent; when that car arrives the call clears, the car goes back to idle and the backings are torn
up.

An emergency re-election advances the term. It happens only between dispatches, never while a car is
already on its way, and every backing collected under the old term is discarded, since the
controllers that gave them are now behind. A controller that is behind is brought up to the running
term by a restamp sweep, after which it can start backing again.

The building engineer has a privileged override: a live call can be killed outright at any moment,
taking the car assignment and all the backings with it, with no vote and no waiting.

The full set of actions is: Press, in which a landing call goes live while none is outstanding;
Back, in which a controller whose stamp matches the running term adds its backing to the live call;
Dispatch, in which a car is sent once a majority backs the call and no car is already moving; Arrive,
in which the moving car reaches the landing and the call, the backings and the car assignment all
clear; Reelect, in which, with no car on its way, the term advances and all backings are torn up;
Restamp, in which every controller that is behind is brought up to the running term; and Override,
in which the building engineer kills the live call, its backings and its car assignment outright.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Whenever a car is on its way to a landing, the backing behind that dispatch is a
majority of the panel and every controller in it still carries the running term stamp, so no
behind-the-term controller ever props up a dispatch in progress.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every landing call that is pressed is eventually cleared, either by a car
arriving or by the engineer's override.

---- MODULE W4Od17m8p4t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Handlers, Chutes, Cap, NoOne

VARIABLES pier, latch, load, alive

vars == <<pier, latch, load, alive>>

Hands == Handlers \cup {NoOne}

\* A held chute latch is a slot already promised to a bag that has not
\* physically landed yet, so it counts against the chute's capacity.
Reserved(ch) == IF latch[ch] # NoOne THEN 1 ELSE 0

TypeOK ==
    /\ pier \in Hands
    /\ latch \in [Chutes -> Hands]
    /\ load \in [Chutes -> 0 .. Cap]
    /\ alive \subseteq Handlers

Init ==
    /\ pier = NoOne
    /\ latch = [ch \in Chutes |-> NoOne]
    /\ load = [ch \in Chutes |-> 0]
    /\ alive = Handlers

\* Coarse before fine: the pier interlock first, then one chute latch.
TakePier(h) ==
    /\ h \in alive
    /\ pier = NoOne
    /\ pier' = h
    /\ UNCHANGED <<latch, load, alive>>

TakeChute(h, ch) ==
    /\ h \in alive
    /\ pier = h
    /\ latch[ch] = NoOne
    /\ load[ch] + 1 <= Cap
    /\ \A k \in Chutes : latch[k] # h
    /\ latch' = [latch EXCEPT ![ch] = h]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pier, load, alive>>

Deposit(h, ch) ==
    /\ h \in alive
    /\ latch[ch] = h
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![ch] = @ + 1]
    /\ latch' = [latch EXCEPT ![ch] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pier, alive>>

DropChute(h, ch) ==
    /\ latch[ch] = h
    /\ latch' = [latch EXCEPT ![ch] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pier, load, alive>>

DropPier(h) ==
    /\ pier = h
    /\ \A ch \in Chutes : latch[ch] # h
    /\ pier' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED <<latch, load, alive>>

Cart(ch) ==
    /\ load[ch] > 0
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![ch] = @ - 1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pier, latch, alive>>

\* A handler can go off the air with no announcement, still holding whatever
\* it had; the reservation it was sitting on is only freed when reclaimed.
Crash(h) ==
    /\ h \in alive
    /\ alive' = alive \ {h}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pier, latch, load>>

Reclaim(h) ==
    /\ h \notin alive
    /\ (pier = h \/ \E ch \in Chutes : latch[ch] = h)
    /\ pier' = IF pier = h THEN NoOne ELSE pier
    /\ latch' = [ch \in Chutes |-> IF latch[ch] = h THEN NoOne ELSE latch[ch]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, alive>>

Restart(h) ==
    /\ h \notin alive
    /\ pier # h
    /\ \A ch \in Chutes : latch[ch] # h
    /\ alive' = alive \cup {h}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<pier, latch, load>>

Next ==
    \/ \E h \in Handlers : TakePier(h) \/ DropPier(h) \/ Crash(h)
    \/ \E h \in Handlers, ch \in Chutes : TakeChute(h, ch) \/ Deposit(h, ch) \/ DropChute(h, ch)
    \/ \E ch \in Chutes : Cart(ch)
    \/ \E h \in Handlers : Reclaim(h) \/ Restart(h)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Bags already in a chute plus the slot promised to whoever holds its latch
\* never exceed what the chute can physically take.
ChuteNeverOversubscribed ==
    \A ch \in Chutes : load[ch] + Reserved(ch) <= Cap

    Chutes = {chBA, chLH}
    Cap = 2

nl:
An airport baggage router feeds bags from the sorter into make-up chutes, one chute per departing
flight. Each chute physically holds a fixed number of bags and no more; pushing a bag into a full
chute jams the belt and stops the whole pier, so the router must never promise a slot it does not
have.

Access is hierarchical. A handler first takes the coarse pier interlock, and only the handler
holding the pier may then take the fine latch on one chute, one chute at a time. Taking a chute
latch is itself a promise: it books a slot for the bag that is about to be pushed, so a latch may
only be taken while the chute has room for the bag already in it plus the one being promised. When
the bag actually lands, the latch is given back and the chute's count goes up by one. A handler that
changes its mind can give the latch back with no bag pushed. The pier interlock is given back once
the handler holds no chute latch. Bags leave chutes the other way when a cart takes one off to the
aircraft.

A handler can crash silently: it simply stops, with no announcement, still holding whatever
interlock and latch it had. Those holds do not evaporate — the slot it booked stays booked until the
supervisor notices and reclaims the dead handler's pier interlock and chute latch. Once nothing is
held in its name, a crashed handler can be restarted.

The full set of actions is: TakePier, in which a live handler takes the free pier interlock;
TakeChute, in which the handler holding the pier books a slot on a chute that has room for it;
Deposit, in which the bag lands, the chute's count rises and the latch is given back; DropChute, in
which a latch is given back with no bag pushed; DropPier, in which a handler holding no latch gives
the pier interlock back; Cart, in which a bag is taken off a chute and out to the aircraft; Crash,
in which a handler stops silently while still holding whatever it held; Reclaim, in which the
supervisor takes back the pier interlock and chute latches held in a crashed handler's name; and
Restart, in which a crashed handler holding nothing is brought back up.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every chute, the bags already in it plus the slot promised to whoever holds its
latch never exceed the chute's physical capacity.

---- MODULE W4Od9m1p5t1 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS RingSize, Zones, Orders, NoOrder

Relays == 0 .. RingSize - 1
Nxt(r) == (r + 1) % RingSize

VARIABLES baton, bus, shed, receipt

vars == <<baton, bus, shed, receipt>>

\* A shed command is broadcast as one copy per relay; the copies travel
\* independently and are picked up in any order.
Copies == [id: Orders, zone: Zones, to: Relays]

For(z) == {m \in bus : m.zone = z}

TypeOK ==
    /\ baton \in Relays
    /\ bus \subseteq Copies
    /\ shed \subseteq Zones
    /\ receipt \in [Zones -> Orders \cup {NoOrder}]

Init ==
    /\ baton = 0
    /\ bus = {}
    /\ shed = {}
    /\ receipt = [z \in Zones |-> NoOrder]

PassBaton ==
    /\ baton' = Nxt(baton)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<bus, shed, receipt>>

\* Only the relay holding the baton may raise a shed order, and only for a zone
\* that is neither already open nor already carrying an order on the bus.
Raise(r, z, k) ==
    /\ baton = r
    /\ shed = {}
    /\ For(z) = {}
    /\ \A m \in bus : m.id # k
    /\ bus' = bus \cup {[id |-> k, zone |-> z, to |-> d] : d \in Relays}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, shed, receipt>>

\* Opening a feeder breaker is one-way for the duration of the event: the
\* copy that lands first is the one written onto the trip receipt.
Trip(m) ==
    /\ m \in bus
    /\ shed = {}
    /\ shed' = {m.zone}
    /\ receipt' = [receipt EXCEPT ![m.zone] = m.id]
    /\ bus' = bus \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED baton

Ignore(m) ==
    /\ m \in bus
    /\ m.zone \in shed
    /\ bus' = bus \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, shed, receipt>>

Restore(z) ==
    /\ z \in shed
    /\ For(z) = {}
    /\ shed' = shed \ {z}
    /\ receipt' = [receipt EXCEPT ![z] = NoOrder]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<baton, bus>>

Ignoring == \E m \in bus : Ignore(m)
Tripping == \E m \in bus : Trip(m)
Restoring == \E z \in Zones : Restore(z)

Next ==
    \/ PassBaton
    \/ \E r \in Relays, z \in Zones, k \in Orders : Raise(r, z, k)
    \/ Tripping \/ Ignoring \/ Restoring

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Tripping) /\ WF_vars(Ignoring) /\ WF_vars(Restoring)

\* Every copy still on the bus for a zone whose breaker is open belongs to the
\* very order that opened it, so no copy can ever open that breaker a second
\* time under a different order.
NoRivalCopy ==
    \A m \in bus : m.zone \in shed => m.id = receipt[m.zone]

\* Shedding is never permanent: an opened zone is always brought back.
GridRecovers == (shed # {}) ~> (shed = {})

CONSTANTS
    RingSize = 3
    Zones = {zNorth, zSouth}
    Orders = {ordA, ordB}
    NoOrder = NoOrder
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoRivalCopy
PROPERTY GridRecovers
nl:
A regional power grid runs an automatic load shedder over a ring of protection relays. When demand
outruns supply the shedder opens the feeder breaker for one grid zone. Opening a breaker is a
one-way act for the duration of the event: the latch stays open until the control room walks it
back, and opening the same zone twice under two different orders would be logged as two separate
outages and would trip the regional interlock, so it must not happen.

Authority to raise a shed order travels with a baton that walks the relay ring one hop at a time.
Only the relay holding the baton may raise an order, and it may do so only when no zone is currently
open and the target zone has no order already on the bus. The order goes out as one copy per relay,
all bearing the same order number, and the copies travel independently: the message bus does not
preserve order, so the copies are picked up in whatever sequence the relays get to them.

Whichever copy is picked up first while no zone is open actually trips the breaker: that zone goes
open and the order number on that copy is written onto the zone's trip receipt. Copies picked up
afterwards for a zone that is already open are recognised as the same order arriving late and are
thrown away rather than acted on. The control room restores a zone once no copies for it are left on
the bus, closing the breaker again and clearing its trip receipt.

The full set of actions is: PassBaton, in which the baton moves one hop round the relay ring; Raise,
in which the baton-holding relay broadcasts one copy per relay of a freshly numbered shed order for
a zone, provided no zone is open and that zone has nothing on the bus; Trip, in which a copy picked
off the bus while no zone is open opens its zone's breaker and writes its order number onto the trip
receipt; Ignore, in which a copy for a zone that is already open is thrown away; and Restore, in
which the control room closes an open zone whose copies have all left the bus and clears its
receipt.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every copy still on the bus addressed to a zone whose breaker is open carries
exactly the order number written on that zone's trip receipt, so no late copy can ever open that
breaker a second time under a different order.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever a zone has been shed, the grid is eventually restored to a state with no
zone open.

---- MODULE W4Od10m3p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Centres, Cabins, Blocks, MaxTerm, Vacant, Nobody

VARIABLES boss, term, claimed, held, stamp

vars == <<boss, term, claimed, held, stamp>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ boss \in [Centres -> Cabins \cup {Nobody}]
    /\ term \in [Centres -> 0 .. MaxTerm]
    /\ claimed \in [Centres -> SUBSET Blocks]
    /\ held \in [Blocks -> Centres \cup {Vacant}]
    /\ stamp \in [Blocks -> 0 .. MaxTerm]

Init ==
    /\ boss = [c \in Centres |-> Nobody]
    /\ term = [c \in Centres |-> 0]
    /\ claimed = [c \in Centres |-> {}]
    /\ held = [b \in Blocks |-> Vacant]
    /\ stamp = [b \in Blocks |-> 0]

\* A fresh election turns the centre's term and drops every claim the previous
\* cabin was working under; blocks it had are left standing but now stale.
Elect(c, k) ==
    /\ boss[c] = Nobody
    /\ boss' = [boss EXCEPT ![c] = k]
    /\ term' = [term EXCEPT ![c] = IF @ = MaxTerm THEN 0 ELSE @ + 1]
    /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![c] = {}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<held, stamp>>

Fail(c) ==
    /\ boss[c] # Nobody
    /\ boss' = [boss EXCEPT ![c] = Nobody]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<term, claimed, held, stamp>>

\* The pool arbiter hands a block to one centre at a time and stamps the grant
\* with the term of the centre it was granted to.
Seize(c, b) ==
    /\ boss[c] # Nobody
    /\ held[b] = Vacant
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![b] = c]
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![b] = term[c]]
    /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![c] = @ \cup {b}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<boss, term>>

Yield(c, b) ==
    /\ b \in claimed[c]
    /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![c] = @ \ {b}]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![b] = Vacant]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<boss, term, stamp>>

\* After a failover the new cabin may pick a block its centre still holds back
\* up, restamping it with the running term before working it.
Readopt(c, b) ==
    /\ boss[c] # Nobody
    /\ held[b] = c
    /\ stamp[b] # term[c]
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![b] = term[c]]
    /\ claimed' = [claimed EXCEPT ![c] = @ \cup {b}]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<boss, term, held>>

Reap(b) ==
    /\ held[b] # Vacant
    /\ boss[held[b]] = Nobody
    /\ b \notin claimed[held[b]]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![b] = Vacant]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<boss, term, claimed, stamp>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Centres, k \in Cabins : Elect(c, k)
    \/ \E c \in Centres : Fail(c)
    \/ \E c \in Centres, b \in Blocks : Seize(c, b) \/ Yield(c, b) \/ Readopt(c, b)
    \/ \E b \in Blocks : Reap(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* A centre only ever works a block the shared arbiter has actually granted to
\* it under the term it is running, so the two centres can never both be
\* working the same block.
ClaimsAreGranted ==
    \A c \in Centres, b \in Blocks :
        b \in claimed[c] => (held[b] = c /\ stamp[b] = term[c])

====
nl:
A subway line is signalled by two independent control centres, a main and a standby, that were built
by different suppliers and share one pool of track blocks. A block is the critical resource: only one
centre may be working a given block at a time, because two centres setting routes over the same
stretch of track would clear conflicting movements onto it.

Each centre runs its own leader election over its cabins. A centre with no cabin in charge elects
one, and the election turns that centre's term. Turning the term drops every claim the previous
cabin was working under, because the new cabin has no idea what the old one was in the middle of.
Blocks the centre was granted are left standing in its name, but their grant stamps are now behind
the centre's term, which marks them as unfinished business rather than live work. A cabin in charge
can fail at any time, leaving its centre leaderless.

The shared pool has a single arbiter. A cabin in charge can seize a vacant block: the arbiter records
which centre now holds it and stamps the grant with that centre's running term, and the block joins
the centre's working claims. A claim is given up by handing the block back to the pool. After a
failover the new cabin can readopt a block its centre still holds by restamping the grant with the
running term and taking it into its working claims. Blocks left standing in the name of a
leaderless centre, and not being worked by it, are reaped back into the pool by the arbiter.

The full set of actions is: Elect, in which a leaderless centre puts a cabin in charge, turns its
term and drops its working claims; Fail, in which the cabin in charge of a centre drops out, leaving
that centre leaderless; Seize, in which a cabin in charge takes a vacant block from the pool, has the
grant stamped with its centre's term and starts working it; Yield, in which a centre stops working a
block and hands it back to the pool; Readopt, in which a new cabin restamps a block its centre still
holds and takes it into its working claims; and Reap, in which the arbiter returns to the pool a
block standing in the name of a leaderless centre that is not being worked.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every block a centre is working has been granted to that very centre by the shared
arbiter and carries a grant stamp equal to the centre's running term, so the two centres can never
both be working the same block.

---- MODULE W4Od15m8p2t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Members, Books, TotalLots, NoOne, NoMove

VARIABLES floor, latch, book, escrow, alive

vars == <<floor, latch, book, escrow, alive>>

Hands == Members \cup {NoOne}
Moves == [from: Books, qty: 1 .. TotalLots]

RECURSIVE Standing(_)
Standing(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET s == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE
         IN book[s] + Standing(S \ {s})

InFlight == IF escrow = NoMove THEN 0 ELSE escrow.qty

TypeOK ==
    /\ floor \in Hands
    /\ latch \in [Books -> Hands]
    /\ book \in [Books -> 0 .. TotalLots]
    /\ escrow \in Moves \cup {NoMove}
    /\ alive \subseteq Members

Init ==
    /\ floor = NoOne
    /\ latch = [s \in Books |-> NoOne]
    /\ book = [s \in Books |-> IF s = CHOOSE x \in Books : TRUE THEN TotalLots ELSE 0]
    /\ escrow = NoMove
    /\ alive = Members

\* Coarse before fine: the auction floor admits one member, and only that
\* member may latch a single order book.
TakeFloor(m) ==
    /\ m \in alive
    /\ floor = NoOne
    /\ floor' = m
    /\ UNCHANGED <<latch, book, escrow, alive>>

TakeBook(m, s) ==
    /\ m \in alive
    /\ floor = m
    /\ latch[s] = NoOne
    /\ \A k \in Books : latch[k] # m
    /\ latch' = [latch EXCEPT ![s] = m]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<floor, book, escrow, alive>>

\* Lots leave the book and sit in escrow; they are never in both places and
\* never in neither.
Lift(m, s, q) ==
    /\ latch[s] = m
    /\ escrow = NoMove
    /\ q <= book[s]
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![s] = @ - q]
    /\ escrow' = [from |-> s, qty |-> q]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<floor, latch, alive>>

Place(s) ==
    /\ escrow # NoMove
    /\ book' = [book EXCEPT ![s] = @ + escrow.qty]
    /\ escrow' = NoMove
    /\ UNCHANGED <<floor, latch, alive>>

Unlatch(m, s) ==
    /\ latch[s] = m
    /\ latch' = [latch EXCEPT ![s] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<floor, book, escrow, alive>>

LeaveFloor(m) ==
    /\ floor = m
    /\ \A s \in Books : latch[s] # m
    /\ floor' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED <<latch, book, escrow, alive>>

\* A member can drop off the network without a word, still holding the floor
\* and a book latch; only the sweep gets them back.
Crash(m) ==
    /\ m \in alive
    /\ alive' = alive \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<floor, latch, book, escrow>>

Sweep(m) ==
    /\ m \notin alive
    /\ (floor = m \/ \E s \in Books : latch[s] = m)
    /\ floor' = IF floor = m THEN NoOne ELSE floor
    /\ latch' = [s \in Books |-> IF latch[s] = m THEN NoOne ELSE latch[s]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<book, escrow, alive>>

Rejoin(m) ==
    /\ m \notin alive
    /\ floor # m
    /\ \A s \in Books : latch[s] # m
    /\ alive' = alive \cup {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<floor, latch, book, escrow>>

Placing == \E s \in Books : Place(s)

Next ==
    \/ \E m \in Members : TakeFloor(m) \/ LeaveFloor(m) \/ Crash(m) \/ Sweep(m) \/ Rejoin(m)
    \/ \E m \in Members, s \in Books : TakeBook(m, s) \/ Unlatch(m, s)
    \/ \E m \in Members, s \in Books, q \in 1 .. TotalLots : Lift(m, s, q)
    \/ Placing

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Placing)

\* Lots only ever move between an order book and escrow, so the lots standing
\* in the books plus the lots in escrow always come to the session total.
LotsConserved == Standing(Books) + InFlight = TotalLots

\* Nothing is left sitting in escrow: a lifted parcel is always placed again.
EscrowDrains == (escrow # NoMove) ~> (escrow = NoMove)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Members = {mAlder, mBirch}
    Books = {bkTelco, bkMiner}
    TotalLots = 2
    NoOne = NoOne
    NoMove = NoMove
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT LotsConserved
PROPERTY EscrowDrains
nl:
A stock exchange runs its opening auction over a small set of order books, one per security. The
session begins with a fixed number of share lots standing in one book and the auction only ever
moves lots between books; nothing is created and nothing is destroyed, so the lots standing in the
books plus whatever is in transit must always come to the session total.

Access is hierarchical. A member firm first takes the auction floor, which admits one firm at a
time, and only the firm on the floor may latch an order book, one book at a time. Moving lots is
done in two steps that never overlap: the firm lifts a parcel out of the book it has latched, which
takes those lots out of the book and puts them into the exchange's escrow, and the parcel is later
placed into a book, which takes it out of escrow and adds it there. Escrow holds at most one parcel
at a time, and a parcel in escrow is always eventually placed. Latches and the floor are given back
in the reverse order they were taken, the floor only once the firm holds no latch.

A member firm can drop off the exchange network without a word, still holding the floor and a book
latch. Nothing it holds is released by the drop itself; the exchange's sweep is what takes the floor
and the latch back, after which the firm can rejoin. A parcel already in escrow when a firm drops
out is unaffected — escrow belongs to the exchange, not to the firm, and it is placed as normal.

The full set of actions is: TakeFloor, in which a live firm takes the free auction floor; TakeBook,
in which the firm on the floor latches a book while holding no other; Lift, in which a firm takes a
parcel out of the book it has latched and into escrow, which must be empty; Place, in which the
parcel in escrow is added to a book and escrow is emptied; Unlatch, in which a firm gives a book
latch back; LeaveFloor, in which a firm holding no latch gives the floor back; Crash, in which a
firm drops off the network silently while still holding the floor and its latch; Sweep, in which the
exchange takes back the floor and latches held in a dropped firm's name; and Rejoin, in which a
dropped firm holding nothing comes back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The lots standing across all order books plus the lots sitting in escrow always
equal the total the session opened with.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every parcel lifted into escrow is eventually placed into a book.

---- MODULE W4Od5m7p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Regions, Lobbies, Rigs, MaxSpin, Empty, NoRig, NoAim

VARIABLES host, placed, aim, spins

vars == <<host, placed, aim, spins>>

Aims == [lob: Lobbies, rig: Rigs]

TypeOK ==
    /\ host \in [Rigs -> Lobbies \cup {Empty}]
    /\ placed \in [Lobbies -> Rigs \cup {NoRig}]
    /\ aim \in [Regions -> Aims \cup {NoAim}]
    /\ spins \in [Regions -> 0 .. MaxSpin]

Init ==
    /\ host = [g \in Rigs |-> Empty]
    /\ placed = [l \in Lobbies |-> NoRig]
    /\ aim = [r \in Regions |-> NoAim]
    /\ spins = [r \in Regions |-> 0]

\* Both matchmaking regions draw from the same rig pool and may line up the
\* same rig for different lobbies; the swap below is what settles it.
Line(r, l, g) ==
    /\ aim[r] = NoAim
    /\ placed[l] = NoRig
    /\ aim' = [aim EXCEPT ![r] = [lob |-> l, rig |-> g]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<host, placed, spins>>

\* The compare-and-swap: the rig must still read empty at the instant of the
\* write, and the lobby must still be unplaced.
Swap(r) ==
    /\ aim[r] # NoAim
    /\ host[aim[r].rig] = Empty
    /\ placed[aim[r].lob] = NoRig
    /\ host' = [host EXCEPT ![aim[r].rig] = aim[r].lob]
    /\ placed' = [placed EXCEPT ![aim[r].lob] = aim[r].rig]
    /\ aim' = [aim EXCEPT ![r] = NoAim]
    /\ UNCHANGED spins

Lost(r) ==
    /\ aim[r] # NoAim
    /\ \/ host[aim[r].rig] # Empty
       \/ placed[aim[r].lob] # NoRig
    /\ spins[r] < MaxSpin
    /\ spins' = [spins EXCEPT ![r] = @ + 1]
    /\ aim' = [aim EXCEPT ![r] = NoAim]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<host, placed>>

Backoff(r) ==
    /\ spins[r] > 0
    /\ spins' = [spins EXCEPT ![r] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<host, placed, aim>>

Teardown(l) ==
    /\ placed[l] # NoRig
    /\ host' = [host EXCEPT ![placed[l]] = Empty]
    /\ placed' = [placed EXCEPT ![l] = NoRig]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<aim, spins>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Regions, l \in Lobbies, g \in Rigs : Line(r, l, g)
    \/ \E r \in Regions : Swap(r) \/ Lost(r) \/ Backoff(r)
    \/ \E l \in Lobbies : Teardown(l)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* The rig a lobby is placed on names that same lobby back, so two lobbies can
\* never end up running on one rig however the two regions interleave.
PlacementIsMutual ==
    \A l \in Lobbies : placed[l] # NoRig => host[placed[l]] = l

====
nl:
A multiplayer game runs two matchmaking regions that were deployed independently but draw game
lobbies onto the same shared pool of server rigs. A rig is the critical resource: it can run one
lobby and one lobby only, and two lobbies landing on the same rig would put two matches' worth of
players into one simulation.

There is no coordinator between the regions. A region lines up a placement by picking an unplaced
lobby and a rig it believes is free, then attempts a compare-and-swap on that rig: the write only
lands if the rig still reads empty at the instant of the attempt and the lobby is still unplaced.
When it lands, the rig records which lobby it is running and the lobby records which rig it is on,
in one step. When it does not land — because the other region got there first, or because the lobby
was placed in the meantime — the attempt is simply lost and the region's spin counter goes up.

Regions back off after spinning: once a region has lost at least one attempt it can reset its spin
counter and start again from a clean slate. The spin counter is capped, so a region cannot keep
losing attempts without backing off.

A lobby's match eventually ends and the placement is torn down, which clears both the rig's record
of the lobby and the lobby's record of the rig, returning the rig to the shared pool.

The full set of actions is: Line, in which a region with no attempt outstanding picks an unplaced
lobby and a rig and lines up a placement; Swap, in which the compare-and-swap lands because the rig
still reads empty and the lobby is still unplaced, writing both records at once; Lost, in which the
attempt fails because the rig is taken or the lobby was placed, and the region's spin counter goes
up; Backoff, in which a region that has spun resets its counter; and Teardown, in which a finished
match clears the lobby's rig and returns the rig to the pool.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every lobby that is placed, the rig it is placed on names that very lobby back,
so no two lobbies can ever be running on the same rig no matter how the two regions interleave.

---- MODULE W4Od2m0p2t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Bays, Bots, Totes, MaxCap, MaxVer, NoPlan

VARIABLES load, ver, carrying, plan, cap

vars == <<load, ver, carrying, plan, cap>>

Plans == [bay: Bays, saw: 0 .. MaxVer]

RECURSIVE Tot(_, _)
Tot(f, S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET x == CHOOSE y \in S : TRUE IN f[x] + Tot(f, S \ {x})

Aloft == Cardinality({r \in Bots : carrying[r]})

TypeOK ==
    /\ load \in [Bays -> 0 .. Totes]
    /\ ver \in [Bays -> 0 .. MaxVer]
    /\ carrying \in [Bots -> BOOLEAN]
    /\ plan \in [Bots -> Plans \cup {NoPlan}]
    /\ cap \in [Bays -> 1 .. MaxCap]

Init ==
    /\ load = [b \in Bays |-> IF b = CHOOSE x \in Bays : TRUE THEN Totes ELSE 0]
    /\ ver = [b \in Bays |-> 0]
    /\ carrying = [r \in Bots |-> FALSE]
    /\ plan = [r \in Bots |-> NoPlan]
    /\ cap = [b \in Bays |-> MaxCap]

Bump(v) == IF v = MaxVer THEN 0 ELSE v + 1

\* Optimistic read: the bot notes the bay's version and walks over without
\* holding anything; the version is rechecked at the moment of the lift.
Scout(r, b) ==
    /\ plan[r] = NoPlan
    /\ ~carrying[r]
    /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![r] = [bay |-> b, saw |-> ver[b]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, ver, carrying, cap>>

\* The aisle takes one tote in motion at a time.
Lift(r) ==
    /\ plan[r] # NoPlan
    /\ ver[plan[r].bay] = plan[r].saw
    /\ load[plan[r].bay] > 0
    /\ \A q \in Bots : ~carrying[q]
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![plan[r].bay] = @ - 1]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![plan[r].bay] = Bump(@)]
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![r] = TRUE]
    /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![r] = NoPlan]
    /\ UNCHANGED cap

Abandon(r) ==
    /\ plan[r] # NoPlan
    /\ \/ ver[plan[r].bay] # plan[r].saw
       \/ load[plan[r].bay] = 0
       \/ \E q \in Bots : carrying[q]
    /\ plan' = [plan EXCEPT ![r] = NoPlan]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, ver, carrying, cap>>

Stow(r, b) ==
    /\ carrying[r]
    /\ load[b] < cap[b]
    /\ load' = [load EXCEPT ![b] = @ + 1]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![b] = Bump(@)]
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![r] = FALSE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, cap>>

\* Racking is re-profiled while the fleet runs, but never below what a bay is
\* already holding and never so far that the floor cannot hold every tote.
Reprofile(b, c) ==
    /\ c >= load[b]
    /\ Tot([k \in Bays |-> IF k = b THEN c ELSE cap[k]], Bays) >= Totes
    /\ cap' = [cap EXCEPT ![b] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<load, ver, carrying, plan>>

Stowing == \E r \in Bots, b \in Bays : Stow(r, b)

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Bots, b \in Bays : Scout(r, b)
    \/ \E r \in Bots : Lift(r) \/ Abandon(r)
    \/ Stowing
    \/ \E b \in Bays, c \in 1 .. MaxCap : Reprofile(b, c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Stowing)

\* Totes are only ever moved between a bay and a bot's cradle, so the totes
\* racked across the floor plus the one in motion always come to the fleet total.
TotesConserved == Tot(load, Bays) + Aloft = Totes

\* A tote lifted off the racking is always racked again.
AisleClears == (\E r \in Bots : carrying[r]) ~> (\A r \in Bots : ~carrying[r])

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Bays = {byNorth, bySouth}
    Bots = {botOne, botTwo}
    Totes = 2
    MaxCap = 2
    MaxVer = 1
    NoPlan = NoPlan
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT TotesConserved
PROPERTY AisleClears
nl:
A warehouse floor is worked by a small fleet of robots that shuttle totes between racking bays. The
floor starts with a fixed number of totes and the robots only ever move them; nothing is added and
nothing is lost, so the totes racked across the bays plus whatever is in motion must always come to
the floor total.

The robots do not lock the bays. A robot scouts a bay optimistically: it notes the bay's version
number and walks over empty-handed. When it gets there it tries to lift a tote, and the lift only
goes ahead if the bay's version is still the one it noted, the bay still has a tote in it, and the
single aisle is clear — the floor allows one tote in motion at a time. A successful lift takes the
tote out of the bay, rolls the bay's version on, and leaves the robot carrying. If any of those
checks fails, the robot abandons the trip and scouts again from scratch. The version number is a
small wrapping field, so it rolls back to zero at the top.

A carrying robot stows its tote into any bay that still has room, which rolls that bay's version on
as well and leaves the robot empty-handed.

The racking itself is re-profiled while the fleet is running. A bay's capacity can be raised or
lowered at any time, but never below the number of totes that bay is already holding, and never so
far that the floor as a whole could not hold every tote — so there is always somewhere to put down
whatever is in motion.

The full set of actions is: Scout, in which an empty-handed robot with no trip planned notes a bay's
version and sets off; Lift, in which a robot takes a tote out of its scouted bay because the version
still matches, the bay is not empty and the aisle is clear, rolling that bay's version on; Abandon,
in which a robot drops a planned trip because the version moved, the bay emptied or the aisle is
busy; Stow, in which a carrying robot puts its tote into a bay that has room, rolling that bay's
version on; and Reprofile, in which a bay's capacity is changed at runtime, never below what it
already holds and never so far that the floor could not hold every tote.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The totes racked across all bays plus the tote in motion always equal the floor
total.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: A tote lifted off the racking is always eventually stowed back into a bay.

---- MODULE W4Od0m8p4t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Surgeons, Theatres, Session, MaxCase, NoOne

VARIABLES daybook, latch, booked, pencilled

vars == <<daybook, latch, booked, pencilled>>

Hands == Surgeons \cup {NoOne}

TypeOK ==
    /\ daybook \in Hands
    /\ latch \in [Theatres -> Hands]
    /\ booked \in [Theatres -> 0 .. Session]
    /\ pencilled \in [Theatres -> 0 .. Session]

Init ==
    /\ daybook = NoOne
    /\ latch = [t \in Theatres |-> NoOne]
    /\ booked = [t \in Theatres |-> 0]
    /\ pencilled = [t \in Theatres |-> 0]

\* Coarse before fine: the day book admits one surgeon, who may then hold the
\* latch on a single theatre.
OpenDaybook(s) ==
    /\ daybook = NoOne
    /\ daybook' = s
    /\ UNCHANGED <<latch, booked, pencilled>>

\* Pencilling in a case reserves its minutes straight away, so the reservation
\* counts against the session before the case is ever confirmed.
Pencil(s, t, d) ==
    /\ daybook = s
    /\ latch[t] = NoOne
    /\ \A k \in Theatres : latch[k] # s
    /\ booked[t] + d <= Session
    /\ latch' = [latch EXCEPT ![t] = s]
    /\ pencilled' = [pencilled EXCEPT ![t] = d]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<daybook, booked>>

Confirm(s, t) ==
    /\ latch[t] = s
    /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![t] = @ + pencilled[t]]
    /\ pencilled' = [pencilled EXCEPT ![t] = 0]
    /\ latch' = [latch EXCEPT ![t] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED daybook

Rub(s, t) ==
    /\ latch[t] = s
    /\ pencilled' = [pencilled EXCEPT ![t] = 0]
    /\ latch' = [latch EXCEPT ![t] = NoOne]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<daybook, booked>>

CloseDaybook(s) ==
    /\ daybook = s
    /\ \A t \in Theatres : latch[t] # s
    /\ daybook' = NoOne
    /\ UNCHANGED <<latch, booked, pencilled>>

\* Privileged override: the clinical director rubs out a pencilled case and
\* frees the theatre latch without asking whoever was holding it.
DirectorClears(t) ==
    /\ latch[t] # NoOne
    /\ latch' = [latch EXCEPT ![t] = NoOne]
    /\ pencilled' = [pencilled EXCEPT ![t] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<daybook, booked>>

DirectorCuts(t, d) ==
    /\ d <= booked[t]
    /\ booked' = [booked EXCEPT ![t] = @ - d]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<daybook, latch, pencilled>>

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Surgeons : OpenDaybook(s) \/ CloseDaybook(s)
    \/ \E s \in Surgeons, t \in Theatres, d \in 1 .. MaxCase : Pencil(s, t, d)
    \/ \E s \in Surgeons, t \in Theatres : Confirm(s, t) \/ Rub(s, t)
    \/ \E t \in Theatres : DirectorClears(t)
    \/ \E t \in Theatres, d \in 1 .. MaxCase : DirectorCuts(t, d)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Confirmed theatre minutes plus the minutes pencilled in behind a held latch
\* never run past the length of the session.
TheatreNotOverbooked ==
    \A t \in Theatres : booked[t] + pencilled[t] <= Session

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Surgeons = {srGrey, srBailey}
    Theatres = {thOrtho, thCardiac}
    Session = 3
    MaxCase = 2
    NoOne = NoOne
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT TheatreNotOverbooked
nl:
A hospital schedules its operating theatres a day at a time. Each theatre has a session of a fixed
number of minutes, and the minutes committed to cases in a theatre must never run past that session:
overrunning means a list that cannot physically be delivered, staff held past their hours and
patients starved for nothing.

Booking is hierarchical. A surgeon first opens the day book, which admits one surgeon at a time, and
only the surgeon holding the day book may take the latch on a theatre, one theatre at a time.
Pencilling a case in takes that latch and reserves the case's minutes there and then, before the
case is confirmed — the reservation counts against the session immediately, so a case can only be
pencilled in if the theatre's already-confirmed minutes leave room for it. Confirming turns the
pencilled minutes into committed minutes and gives the latch back. Rubbing the case out gives the
latch back with nothing committed. The day book is closed once the surgeon holds no theatre latch.

The clinical director has a privileged override on both halves of this. The director can clear a
theatre outright, rubbing out whatever is pencilled in and freeing the latch without asking the
surgeon holding it. The director can also cut minutes back out of a theatre's committed list, which
is how an emergency is made room for once cases have already been confirmed.

The full set of actions is: OpenDaybook, in which a surgeon takes the free day book; Pencil, in
which the surgeon holding the day book takes a free theatre latch and reserves a case's minutes
against a session that has room for them; Confirm, in which the pencilled minutes become committed
minutes and the latch is given back; Rub, in which the pencilled case is dropped and the latch given
back with nothing committed; CloseDaybook, in which a surgeon holding no latch gives the day book
back; DirectorClears, in which the clinical director frees a theatre latch and rubs out whatever was
pencilled in behind it; and DirectorCuts, in which the director removes committed minutes from a
theatre's list.

SAFETY PROPERTY: For every theatre, the minutes already committed plus the minutes pencilled in
behind a held latch never exceed the length of that theatre's session.

---- MODULE W4Od17m7p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Routers, Lanes, MaxWave, Free, NoLane

VARIABLES reg, claim, attempt, wave

vars == <<reg, claim, attempt, wave>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in [Lanes -> Routers \cup {Free}]
    /\ claim \in [Routers -> SUBSET Lanes]
    /\ attempt \in [Routers -> Lanes \cup {NoLane}]
    /\ wave \in 0 .. MaxWave

Init ==
    /\ reg = [n \in Lanes |-> Free]
    /\ claim = [r \in Routers |-> {}]
    /\ attempt = [r \in Routers |-> NoLane]
    /\ wave = 0

\* Both routers were commissioned separately and both draw from the same lane
\* pool, so they routinely line up the same lane.
Aim(r, n) ==
    /\ attempt[r] = NoLane
    /\ n \notin claim[r]
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![r] = n]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, claim, wave>>

\* The compare-and-swap: the lane register must still read free at the instant
\* the router writes its own name into it.
Swap(r) ==
    /\ attempt[r] # NoLane
    /\ reg[attempt[r]] = Free
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![attempt[r]] = r]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![r] = @ \cup {attempt[r]}]
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![r] = NoLane]
    /\ UNCHANGED wave

Miss(r) ==
    /\ attempt[r] # NoLane
    /\ reg[attempt[r]] # Free
    /\ attempt' = [attempt EXCEPT ![r] = NoLane]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, claim, wave>>

Yield(r, n) ==
    /\ n \in claim[r]
    /\ claim' = [claim EXCEPT ![r] = @ \ {n}]
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![n] = Free]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<attempt, wave>>

\* The sorter works in waves: at the end of one, every lane register is
\* cleared down and both routers start the next wave holding nothing.
Flush ==
    /\ \E r \in Routers : claim[r] # {}
    /\ reg' = [n \in Lanes |-> Free]
    /\ claim' = [r \in Routers |-> {}]
    /\ wave' = IF wave = MaxWave THEN 0 ELSE wave + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED attempt

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Routers, n \in Lanes : Aim(r, n) \/ Yield(r, n)
    \/ \E r \in Routers : Swap(r) \/ Miss(r)
    \/ Flush

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Flush)

\* No lane is ever being worked by both routers at once.
LanesNotShared ==
    \A a, b \in Routers : a # b => claim[a] \cap claim[b] = {}

\* Every wave is cleared down: lanes never stay held for ever.
WavesClearDown ==
    (\E r \in Routers : claim[r] # {}) ~> (\A r \in Routers : claim[r] = {})

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Routers = {rtTerminalA, rtTerminalB}
    Lanes = {lnTransfer, lnLocal}
    MaxWave = 1
    Free = Free
    NoLane = NoLane
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT LanesNotShared
PROPERTY WavesClearDown
nl:
An airport's baggage router is really two routers: each terminal was commissioned separately with its
own sortation controller, and both feed the same shared pool of transfer lanes under the apron. A
lane is a critical resource — a lane being worked by two controllers at once means two streams of
bags interleaved on one belt and a jam under the terminal — so a lane must never be held by both at
the same time.

There is no arbiter between the two controllers. A controller lines up a lane it is not already
working, then attempts a compare-and-swap on that lane's register: the write only lands if the
register still reads free at the instant of the attempt, and when it lands the controller's own name
goes into the register and the lane joins the set the controller is working. If the register no
longer reads free — because the other terminal got there first — the attempt is missed and the
controller lines something else up. A controller can also yield a lane it is working, which clears
the register back to free.

The sorter runs in waves. At the end of a wave every lane register is cleared down at once, both
controllers are left working nothing, and the wave counter rolls on, wrapping at the top of its
range. A wave always ends: lanes are never held indefinitely.

The full set of actions is: Aim, in which a controller with no attempt outstanding lines up a lane
it is not already working; Swap, in which the compare-and-swap lands because the register still
reads free, writing the controller's name into it and adding the lane to what that controller is
working; Miss, in which the attempt is dropped because the register no longer reads free; Yield, in
which a controller gives up a lane it is working and the register goes back to free; and Flush, in
which the wave ends, every register is cleared down, both controllers are left working nothing and
the wave counter rolls on.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No lane is ever in the set of lanes being worked by both controllers at the same
time.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever either controller is working a lane, the sorter eventually reaches a
point where neither controller is working any lane.

---- MODULE W4Od10m2p6t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cabins, Points, MaxPlan, Normal, NoBid

VARIABLES thrown, plan, up, ballot, bid

vars == <<thrown, plan, up, ballot, bid>>

Throws == [cab: Cabins, ep: 0 .. MaxPlan]
Bids == [pt: Points, by: Cabins]

TypeOK ==
    /\ thrown \in [Points -> Throws \cup {Normal}]
    /\ plan \in 0 .. MaxPlan
    /\ up \subseteq Cabins
    /\ ballot \in [Cabins -> {"none", "yes", "no"}]
    /\ bid \in Bids \cup {NoBid}

Init ==
    /\ thrown = [p \in Points |-> Normal]
    /\ plan = 0
    /\ up = Cabins
    /\ ballot = [c \in Cabins |-> "none"]
    /\ bid = NoBid

Propose(c, p) ==
    /\ bid = NoBid
    /\ c \in up
    /\ thrown[p] = Normal
    /\ bid' = [pt |-> p, by |-> c]
    /\ ballot' = [k \in Cabins |-> "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<thrown, plan, up>>

\* Only a cabin that is still on the air votes; a cabin that has dropped out
\* silently is simply not counted either way.
Aye(c) ==
    /\ bid # NoBid
    /\ c \in up
    /\ ballot[c] = "none"
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![c] = "yes"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<thrown, plan, up, bid>>

Nay(c) ==
    /\ bid # NoBid
    /\ c \in up
    /\ ballot[c] = "none"
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![c] = "no"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<thrown, plan, up, bid>>

\* The commit stamps the throw with the plan epoch it was decided under.
Commit ==
    /\ bid # NoBid
    /\ bid.by \in up
    /\ \A c \in up : ballot[c] = "yes"
    /\ thrown' = [thrown EXCEPT ![bid.pt] = [cab |-> bid.by, ep |-> plan]]
    /\ bid' = NoBid
    /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, up, ballot>>

Abort ==
    /\ bid # NoBid
    /\ \/ bid.by \notin up
       \/ \E c \in up : ballot[c] = "no"
    /\ bid' = NoBid
    /\ UNCHANGED <<thrown, plan, up, ballot>>

Restore(p) ==
    /\ thrown[p] # Normal
    /\ thrown' = [thrown EXCEPT ![p] = Normal]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, up, ballot, bid>>

\* A cabin can go off the air with no warning; its throws stay in the field
\* until the fail-safe puts them back to normal.
Drop(c) ==
    /\ c \in up
    /\ up' = up \ {c}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<thrown, plan, ballot, bid>>

Failsafe(p) ==
    /\ thrown[p] # Normal
    /\ thrown[p].cab \notin up
    /\ thrown' = [thrown EXCEPT ![p] = Normal]
    /\ bid' = NoBid
    /\ UNCHANGED <<plan, up, ballot>>

Rejoin(c) ==
    /\ c \notin up
    /\ up' = up \cup {c}
    /\ ballot' = [ballot EXCEPT ![c] = "none"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<thrown, plan, bid>>

\* A new signalling plan supersedes every throw decided under the old one, so
\* the whole layout is put back to normal as the epoch turns.
Replan ==
    /\ plan' = IF plan = MaxPlan THEN 0 ELSE plan + 1
    /\ thrown' = [p \in Points |-> Normal]
    /\ bid' = NoBid
    /\ UNCHANGED <<up, ballot>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cabins, p \in Points : Propose(c, p)
    \/ \E c \in Cabins : Aye(c) \/ Nay(c) \/ Drop(c) \/ Rejoin(c)
    \/ Commit \/ Abort \/ Replan
    \/ \E p \in Points : Restore(p) \/ Failsafe(p)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No point machine is ever left thrown under a signalling plan that has since
\* been superseded, so nothing in the field is acting on a stale decision.
NoStaleThrow ==
    \A p \in Points : thrown[p] # Normal => thrown[p].ep = plan

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Cabins = {cbNorth, cbSouth}
    Points = {ptCrossover, ptSiding}
    MaxPlan = 1
    Normal = Normal
    NoBid = NoBid
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoStaleThrow
nl:
A subway line sets routes by agreement between its interlocking cabins rather than from a single
box. Throwing a point machine is decided by two-phase commit: a cabin proposes a point that is
currently lying normal, every cabin still on the air votes, and the throw only goes ahead if all of
them vote in favour and the proposing cabin is still on the air. A single vote against, or the
proposer dropping out, aborts the round with nothing thrown. Only one proposal is on the table at a
time.

The line runs against a signalling plan, and every throw that goes ahead is stamped with the plan
epoch it was decided under, along with the cabin that proposed it. The safety case turns on that
stamp: a point left thrown under a plan that has since been superseded is a point set by a decision
nobody would take today, and it must not be left in the field. So when the line is replanned, the
epoch turns and the whole layout is put back to normal in the same movement, and any proposal on the
table is dropped.

A cabin can go off the air with no warning at all — no message, no handover. Its votes simply stop
being collected, but the points it threw stay thrown in the field until the fail-safe notices the
cabin is gone and puts them back to normal. Points can also be restored to normal in the ordinary
course of running trains. A cabin that comes back on the air rejoins with a cleared ballot.

The full set of actions is: Propose, in which a cabin on the air puts a normal point on the table
and clears the ballot; Aye and Nay, in which a cabin on the air casts its single vote for or against
the proposal; Commit, in which a unanimous ballot among the cabins on the air throws the point,
stamped with the proposing cabin and the running plan epoch; Abort, in which a vote against or the
proposer dropping out ends the round with nothing thrown; Restore, in which a thrown point is put
back to normal in ordinary running; Drop, in which a cabin goes off the air silently; Failsafe, in
which points thrown in the name of a cabin that is off the air are put back to normal and the
proposal on the table is dropped; Rejoin, in which a cabin comes back on the air with a cleared
ballot; and Replan, in which the signalling plan epoch turns, the whole layout is put back to normal
and any proposal is dropped.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No point machine is ever left thrown carrying a plan epoch other than the one the
line is currently running, so nothing in the field is standing on a superseded decision.
