---- MODULE W4Od11m0p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Spoolers, Presses, MaxVer, MaxRetry, Free, NoNote, NoTicket

VARIABLES holder, stamp, note, ticket, retries

vars == <<holder, stamp, note, ticket, retries>>

Notes == [press: Presses, saw: 0 .. MaxVer]
Tickets == [press: Presses, ep: 0 .. MaxVer]

Roll(v) == IF v = MaxVer THEN 0 ELSE v + 1

TypeOK ==
    /\ holder \in [Presses -> Spoolers \cup {Free}]
    /\ stamp \in [Presses -> 0 .. MaxVer]
    /\ note \in [Spoolers -> Notes \cup {NoNote}]
    /\ ticket \in [Spoolers -> Tickets \cup {NoTicket}]
    /\ retries \in [Spoolers -> 0 .. MaxRetry]

Init ==
    /\ holder = [p \in Presses |-> Free]
    /\ stamp = [p \in Presses |-> 0]
    /\ note = [s \in Spoolers |-> NoNote]
    /\ ticket = [s \in Spoolers |-> NoTicket]
    /\ retries = [s \in Spoolers |-> 0]

\* Optimistic read: the spooler writes down the press stamp it saw and does not
\* hold anything while it prepares the job.
Peek(s, p) ==
    /\ note[s] = NoNote
    /\ ticket[s] = NoTicket
    /\ note' = [note EXCEPT ![s] = [press |-> p, saw |-> stamp[p]]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, stamp, ticket, retries>>

\* The claim goes through only if the press is still unheld and its stamp has
\* not moved since the read; the shop's single ink line allows one live job.
Claim(s) ==
    /\ note[s] # NoNote
    /\ holder[note[s].press] = Free
    /\ stamp[note[s].press] = note[s].saw
    /\ \A q \in Spoolers : ticket[q] = NoTicket
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![note[s].press] = s]
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![note[s].press] = Roll(@)]
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![s] = [press |-> note[s].press,
                                        ep |-> Roll(stamp[note[s].press])]]
    /\ note' = [note EXCEPT ![s] = NoNote]
    /\ UNCHANGED retries

Lapse(s) ==
    /\ note[s] # NoNote
    /\ \/ holder[note[s].press] # Free
       \/ stamp[note[s].press] # note[s].saw
       \/ \E q \in Spoolers : ticket[q] # NoTicket
    /\ retries[s] < MaxRetry
    /\ retries' = [retries EXCEPT ![s] = @ + 1]
    /\ note' = [note EXCEPT ![s] = NoNote]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, stamp, ticket>>

Settle(s) ==
    /\ retries[s] > 0
    /\ retries' = [retries EXCEPT ![s] = 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, stamp, note, ticket>>

Finish(s) ==
    /\ ticket[s] # NoTicket
    /\ holder' = [holder EXCEPT ![ticket[s].press] = Free]
    /\ stamp' = [stamp EXCEPT ![ticket[s].press] = Roll(@)]
    /\ ticket' = [ticket EXCEPT ![s] = NoTicket]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<note, retries>>

Finishing == \E s \in Spoolers : Finish(s)

Next ==
    \/ \E s \in Spoolers, p \in Presses : Peek(s, p)
    \/ \E s \in Spoolers : Claim(s) \/ Lapse(s) \/ Settle(s)
    \/ Finishing

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Finishing)

\* A spooler only ever runs a press that is recorded as held by it and whose
\* stamp still reads the value written when the claim went through, so two
\* spoolers can never both be running the same press.
TicketMatchesPress ==
    \A s \in Spoolers :
        ticket[s] # NoTicket =>
            /\ holder[ticket[s].press] = s
            /\ stamp[ticket[s].press] = ticket[s].ep

\* No job holds a press for ever: the shop always comes back to idle.
PressesFreeUp ==
    (\E s \in Spoolers : ticket[s] # NoTicket) ~> (\A s \in Spoolers : ticket[s] = NoTicket)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Spoolers = {spDesign, spRepro}
    Presses = {prLitho, prDigital}
    MaxVer = 1
    MaxRetry = 1
    Free = Free
    NoNote = NoNote
    NoTicket = NoTicket
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT TicketMatchesPress
PROPERTY PressesFreeUp
nl:
A commercial print shop runs two job spoolers that were installed years apart and never taught about
each other. Both queue work onto the same pool of presses. A press is a critical resource: two
spoolers driving the same press means two jobs interleaved on one sheet feed and a ruined run, so a
press must never be run by both at once.

Neither spooler takes a lock up front. A spooler peeks at a press, writing down the stamp the press
is showing, and then goes away and prepares the job. When it comes back it tries to claim: the claim
only goes through if the press is still unheld, its stamp has not moved since the peek, and no job
is live anywhere in the shop — there is a single ink line, so one press runs at a time. A successful
claim records the spooler as the press's holder, rolls the press stamp on, and hands the spooler a
ticket naming the press and the stamp value the claim left behind. The stamp is a small wrapping
counter that rolls back to zero at the top.

If the press was taken, or the stamp moved while the job was being prepared, or another job is live,
the attempt lapses and the spooler's retry count goes up. The retry count is capped and a spooler
settles back to zero before going round again. When a job finishes, the press is released, the stamp
rolls on once more and the ticket is given up.

The full set of actions is: Peek, in which a spooler holding neither a note nor a ticket writes down
a press's current stamp; Claim, in which the attempt goes through because the press is unheld, its
stamp is unmoved and no job is live, recording the holder, rolling the stamp and issuing a ticket;
Lapse, in which the attempt fails and the spooler's retry count goes up; Settle, in which a spooler
resets its retry count; and Finish, in which a live job ends, releasing the press, rolling its stamp
and giving up the ticket.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every spooler holding a ticket is running a press that records that very spooler as
its holder and whose stamp still reads the value the claim left behind, so two spoolers can never
both be running the same press.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Whenever a job is live on a press, the shop eventually comes back to a state
where no spooler holds a ticket.

---- MODULE W4Od10m7p6t5 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Gangs, Sections, MaxTok, Clear, NoSec

VARIABLES reg, owner, tok, onTrack, onDuty

vars == <<reg, owner, tok, onTrack, onDuty>>

Roll(v) == IF v = MaxTok THEN 0 ELSE v + 1

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in [Sections -> 0 .. MaxTok]
    /\ owner \in [Sections -> Gangs \cup {Clear}]
    /\ tok \in [Gangs -> 0 .. MaxTok]
    /\ onTrack \in [Gangs -> Sections \cup {NoSec}]
    /\ onDuty \subseteq Gangs

Init ==
    /\ reg = [s \in Sections |-> 0]
    /\ owner = [s \in Sections |-> Clear]
    /\ tok = [g \in Gangs |-> 0]
    /\ onTrack = [g \in Gangs |-> NoSec]
    /\ onDuty = Gangs

\* The possession register is swapped from clear to the gang's name and rolled
\* on in one step; the gang keeps the value the swap left behind.
Grant(g, s) ==
    /\ g \in onDuty
    /\ owner[s] = Clear
    /\ onTrack[g] = NoSec
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = g]
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = Roll(@)]
    /\ tok' = [tok EXCEPT ![g] = Roll(reg[s])]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<onTrack, onDuty>>

\* A gang steps onto the ballast only while its token still matches the
\* section register, which is what makes the possession current rather than stale.
Enter(g, s) ==
    /\ g \in onDuty
    /\ onTrack[g] = NoSec
    /\ owner[s] = g
    /\ tok[g] = reg[s]
    /\ onTrack' = [onTrack EXCEPT ![g] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, owner, tok, onDuty>>

Leave(g) ==
    /\ onTrack[g] # NoSec
    /\ onTrack' = [onTrack EXCEPT ![g] = NoSec]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, owner, tok, onDuty>>

\* Handing a possession back is itself a swap, and a gang whose token has been
\* superseded cannot do it -- it no longer speaks for that section.
HandBack(g, s) ==
    /\ g \in onDuty
    /\ owner[s] = g
    /\ tok[g] = reg[s]
    /\ onTrack[g] # s
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = Clear]
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = Roll(@)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tok, onTrack, onDuty>>

\* Privileged override: the signaller takes a section back for a train, rolls
\* the register past whatever token is out there and clears the ballast.
Revoke(s) ==
    /\ owner[s] # Clear
    /\ owner' = [owner EXCEPT ![s] = Clear]
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![s] = Roll(@)]
    /\ onTrack' = [g \in Gangs |-> IF onTrack[g] = s THEN NoSec ELSE onTrack[g]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<tok, onDuty>>

StandDown(g) ==
    /\ g \in onDuty
    /\ onDuty' = onDuty \ {g}
    /\ onTrack' = [onTrack EXCEPT ![g] = NoSec]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, owner, tok>>

SignOn(g) ==
    /\ g \notin onDuty
    /\ onDuty' = onDuty \cup {g}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, owner, tok, onTrack>>

Next ==
    \/ \E g \in Gangs, s \in Sections : Grant(g, s) \/ Enter(g, s) \/ HandBack(g, s)
    \/ \E g \in Gangs : Leave(g) \/ StandDown(g) \/ SignOn(g)
    \/ \E s \in Sections : Revoke(s)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Anyone found on the ballast is booked on duty, named on that section's
\* possession register, and holding the token the register currently reads.
NobodyStaleOnTrack ==
    \A g \in Gangs :
        onTrack[g] # NoSec =>
            /\ g \in onDuty
            /\ owner[onTrack[g]] = g
            /\ tok[g] = reg[onTrack[g]]

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Gangs = {gnRail, gnSignals}
    Sections = {secCutting, secTunnel}
    MaxTok = 2
    Clear = Clear
    NoSec = NoSec
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NobodyStaleOnTrack
nl:
Engineering work on a subway line is protected by possessions. Before a gang may stand on the
ballast in a track section, that section's possession register must have been swapped from clear to
that gang's name, and the swap rolls the register on to a new value which the gang keeps as its
token. The register is a small wrapping counter, so it rolls back to zero at the top of its range.

The safety case is about who is standing where. A gang may step onto a section only while it is
booked on duty, the section's register still names it, and the token it kept still reads the same as
the register. That last check is what makes a possession current rather than superseded: any gang
holding a token the register has since rolled past is speaking for a possession that no longer
exists, and must not be on the track. Handing a possession back is itself a swap and is subject to
the same check, so a gang whose token has been superseded cannot hand back a section it no longer
speaks for.

The signaller has a privileged override. A section can be taken back at any moment to run a train:
the register is rolled past whatever token is out there, the section goes clear, and anybody standing
in it is cleared off the ballast in the same movement.

Gangs also come and go from shift. Standing down takes a gang off duty and off the ballast at once,
though any possession still in its name is left standing until the signaller takes it back. A gang
that signs back on is on duty again but holds whatever token it had before.

The full set of actions is: Grant, in which a clear section's register is swapped to an on-duty
gang's name, rolled on, and the new value kept by that gang as its token; Enter, in which an on-duty
gang whose token matches the register of a section it is named on steps onto the ballast; Leave, in
which a gang steps off the ballast; HandBack, in which an on-duty gang holding a current token and
not standing in the section clears the register and rolls it on; Revoke, in which the signaller takes
a section back, rolls the register on and clears anybody out of it; StandDown, in which a gang goes
off duty and off the ballast; and SignOn, in which a gang comes back on duty.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every gang standing on the ballast is booked on duty, is named on that section's
possession register, and holds a token equal to what the register currently reads, so nobody off
duty and nobody holding a superseded possession is ever on the track.

---- MODULE W4Od10m7p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Crossovers, Free, Ash, Black, NoAim

VARIABLES reg, aimAsh, aimBlack, setAsh, setBlack

vars == <<reg, aimAsh, aimBlack, setAsh, setBlack>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in [Crossovers -> {Free, Ash, Black}]
    /\ aimAsh \in Crossovers \cup {NoAim}
    /\ aimBlack \in Crossovers \cup {NoAim}
    /\ setAsh \subseteq Crossovers
    /\ setBlack \subseteq Crossovers

Init ==
    /\ reg = [x \in Crossovers |-> Free]
    /\ aimAsh = NoAim
    /\ aimBlack = NoAim
    /\ setAsh = {}
    /\ setBlack = {}

\* Ashfield box.  It lines a crossover up, then swaps the register from free to
\* its own name; the swap is the only thing standing between the two boxes.
LineAsh(x) ==
    /\ aimAsh = NoAim
    /\ x \notin setAsh
    /\ aimAsh' = x
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, aimBlack, setAsh, setBlack>>

SwapAsh ==
    /\ aimAsh # NoAim
    /\ reg[aimAsh] = Free
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![aimAsh] = Ash]
    /\ setAsh' = setAsh \cup {aimAsh}
    /\ aimAsh' = NoAim
    /\ UNCHANGED <<aimBlack, setBlack>>

MissAsh ==
    /\ aimAsh # NoAim
    /\ reg[aimAsh] # Free
    /\ aimAsh' = NoAim
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, aimBlack, setAsh, setBlack>>

DropAsh(x) ==
    /\ x \in setAsh
    /\ setAsh' = setAsh \ {x}
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![x] = Free]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<aimAsh, aimBlack, setBlack>>

\* Blackford box.  Same protocol, separate equipment, no link to Ashfield
\* except the shared register on each crossover.
LineBlack(x) ==
    /\ aimBlack = NoAim
    /\ x \notin setBlack
    /\ aimBlack' = x
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, aimAsh, setAsh, setBlack>>

SwapBlack ==
    /\ aimBlack # NoAim
    /\ reg[aimBlack] = Free
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![aimBlack] = Black]
    /\ setBlack' = setBlack \cup {aimBlack}
    /\ aimBlack' = NoAim
    /\ UNCHANGED <<aimAsh, setAsh>>

MissBlack ==
    /\ aimBlack # NoAim
    /\ reg[aimBlack] # Free
    /\ aimBlack' = NoAim
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, aimAsh, setAsh, setBlack>>

DropBlack(x) ==
    /\ x \in setBlack
    /\ setBlack' = setBlack \ {x}
    /\ reg' = [reg EXCEPT ![x] = Free]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<aimAsh, aimBlack, setAsh>>

ResolveAsh == SwapAsh \/ MissAsh
ResolveBlack == SwapBlack \/ MissBlack

Next ==
    \/ \E x \in Crossovers : LineAsh(x) \/ DropAsh(x) \/ LineBlack(x) \/ DropBlack(x)
    \/ ResolveAsh \/ ResolveBlack

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(ResolveAsh) /\ WF_vars(ResolveBlack)

\* Each box only ever holds crossovers whose register carries its own name, so
\* the two boxes can never both hold the same crossover.
RoutesNotShared ==
    /\ \A x \in setAsh : reg[x] = Ash
    /\ \A x \in setBlack : reg[x] = Black

\* Neither box is left with an attempt hanging: every line-up is settled.
AttemptsSettle ==
    /\ (aimAsh # NoAim) ~> (aimAsh = NoAim)
    /\ (aimBlack # NoAim) ~> (aimBlack = NoAim)

CONSTANTS
    Crossovers = {xNorthJn, xDepot, xCarriageSdg}
    Free = Free
    Ash = Ash
    Black = Black
    NoAim = NoAim
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT RoutesNotShared
PROPERTY AttemptsSettle
nl:
Two signal boxes, Ashfield and Blackford, were built decades apart and control adjoining stretches of
the same subway line. Neither knows the other exists in software, but both need the same handful of
crossovers, which sit in a shared pool between them. A crossover is a critical resource: two boxes
holding the same crossover means two conflicting routes over one set of blades, so no crossover may
ever be held by both boxes at once.

There is nothing between them but a register on each crossover, which reads free or carries the name
of whichever box holds it. A box works in two steps. First it lines a crossover up — picking one it
is not already holding and noting it as the target of its next attempt. Then it swaps: the write
lands only if the register still reads free at that instant, and when it lands the box's own name
goes into the register and the crossover joins the set that box is holding. If the register is no
longer free, because the other box got in first, the attempt is missed and the target is dropped.
Neither box lets an attempt hang: a lined-up crossover is always either swapped or missed.

A box drops a crossover it is holding when the route through it is no longer needed, which puts the
register back to free and returns the crossover to the shared pool.

The full set of actions is: LineAsh and LineBlack, in which the box concerned, having no attempt
outstanding, targets a crossover it is not already holding; SwapAsh and SwapBlack, in which the
attempt lands because the register still reads free, writing that box's name in and adding the
crossover to what it holds; MissAsh and MissBlack, in which the attempt is dropped because the
register is no longer free; and DropAsh and DropBlack, in which a box gives up a crossover it holds
and the register goes back to free.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every crossover held by Ashfield carries Ashfield's name in its register and every
crossover held by Blackford carries Blackford's, so the two boxes can never both be holding the same
crossover.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Neither box is ever left with an attempt hanging: any crossover a box has lined up
is eventually either swapped to it or missed.

---- MODULE W4Od1m6p3t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Desks, Flights, Slots, Horizon, MaxLease, Vacant, NoSlot

VARIABLES lease, clock, cleared, staffed

vars == <<lease, clock, cleared, staffed>>

Leases == [to: Flights, until: 1 .. Horizon]

Live(s) == lease[s] # Vacant /\ lease[s].until > clock

TypeOK ==
    /\ lease \in [Slots -> Leases \cup {Vacant}]
    /\ clock \in 0 .. Horizon
    /\ cleared \in [Flights -> Slots \cup {NoSlot}]
    /\ staffed \subseteq Desks

Init ==
    /\ lease = [s \in Slots |-> Vacant]
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ cleared = [f \in Flights |-> NoSlot]
    /\ staffed = Desks

\* A slot is let on a lease with a wall-clock expiry rather than handed over
\* outright, so a desk that goes quiet cannot hold a slot for ever.
Let(d, s, f, len) ==
    /\ d \in staffed
    /\ ~Live(s)
    /\ cleared[f] = NoSlot
    /\ \A k \in Slots : lease[k] # Vacant => lease[k].to # f
    /\ clock + len <= Horizon
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![s] = [to |-> f, until |-> clock + len]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, cleared, staffed>>

Extend(d, s, len) ==
    /\ d \in staffed
    /\ Live(s)
    /\ clock + len <= Horizon
    /\ lease[s].until < clock + len
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![s] = [to |-> @.to, until |-> clock + len]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, cleared, staffed>>

Clear(f, s) ==
    /\ cleared[f] = NoSlot
    /\ Live(s)
    /\ lease[s].to = f
    /\ cleared' = [cleared EXCEPT ![f] = s]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, clock, staffed>>

Roll(f) ==
    /\ cleared[f] # NoSlot
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![cleared[f]] = Vacant]
    /\ cleared' = [cleared EXCEPT ![f] = NoSlot]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, staffed>>

\* Clearance lapses with the lease: the minute a lease runs out, the flight
\* holding it is taken off the departure list in the same movement.
Tick ==
    /\ clock < Horizon
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ cleared' = [f \in Flights |->
                       IF cleared[f] # NoSlot /\ lease[cleared[f]].until <= clock + 1
                       THEN NoSlot ELSE cleared[f]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, staffed>>

Reap(s) ==
    /\ lease[s] # Vacant
    /\ lease[s].until <= clock
    /\ lease' = [lease EXCEPT ![s] = Vacant]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, cleared, staffed>>

\* A desk can go quiet with no handover; the leases it let simply run out.
GoQuiet(d) ==
    /\ d \in staffed
    /\ staffed' = staffed \ {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, clock, cleared>>

ComeBack(d) ==
    /\ d \notin staffed
    /\ staffed' = staffed \cup {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, clock, cleared>>

NewDay ==
    /\ \A s \in Slots : lease[s] = Vacant
    /\ \A f \in Flights : cleared[f] = NoSlot
    /\ clock' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lease, cleared, staffed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E d \in Desks, s \in Slots, f \in Flights, n \in 1 .. MaxLease : Let(d, s, f, n)
    \/ \E d \in Desks, s \in Slots, n \in 1 .. MaxLease : Extend(d, s, n)
    \/ \E f \in Flights, s \in Slots : Clear(f, s)
    \/ \E f \in Flights : Roll(f)
    \/ \E s \in Slots : Reap(s)
    \/ \E d \in Desks : GoQuiet(d) \/ ComeBack(d)
    \/ Tick \/ NewDay

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every flight on the departure list is standing on a slot lease that names
\* that very flight and has not yet run out, so no slot is ever handed to two
\* flights at once.
ClearanceBackedByLease ==
    \A f \in Flights :
        cleared[f] # NoSlot =>
            /\ lease[cleared[f]] # Vacant
            /\ lease[cleared[f]].to = f
            /\ lease[cleared[f]].until > clock

====
nl:
An airport allocates departure slots on its single runway. A slot is let to one flight and one
flight only; two flights holding the same slot means two aircraft rolling for the same window, so a
double allocation is the thing the allocator exists to prevent.

Slots are not handed over outright, they are let on leases with a wall-clock expiry. A staffed
control desk lets a slot to a flight for a chosen number of minutes, provided the slot is not
already under a live lease, the flight does not already hold a lease elsewhere, and the expiry falls
inside the day's horizon. A desk can extend a live lease to a later expiry, again within the
horizon. When a lease runs out it is reaped and the slot goes back into the pool.

A flight is put on the departure list only against a live lease that names it. Clearance lapses with
the lease: as the clock ticks past a lease's expiry, any flight standing on that lease comes off the
departure list in the same movement, so nobody is ever left cleared on a lease that has run out. A
flight that actually rolls comes off the list and its lease is torn up.

A control desk can go quiet with no handover at all — no message, no transfer of its bookings. That
is exactly what the expiry is for: leases the quiet desk let simply run out on their own and the
slots return to the pool without anybody having to intervene. A desk that comes back can let slots
again. When the runway is quiet — no live leases, nobody on the departure list — the clock is reset
for a new day.

The full set of actions is: Let, in which a staffed desk lets a free slot to a flight that holds no
other lease, with an expiry inside the horizon; Extend, in which a staffed desk pushes a live lease's
expiry later; Clear, in which a flight is put on the departure list against a live lease naming it;
Roll, in which a cleared flight departs, coming off the list and tearing up its lease; Reap, in which
a lease that has run out is cleared away; GoQuiet, in which a desk stops working with no handover;
ComeBack, in which a quiet desk resumes; Tick, in which the clock advances a minute and any flight
whose lease has just run out comes off the departure list; and NewDay, in which the clock is reset
once no leases are live and nobody is cleared.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every flight on the departure list stands on a slot lease that names that very
flight and has not yet run out, so a slot can never be allocated to two flights at the same time.

---- MODULE W4Od4m9p0t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Bays, MaxEpoch, NoBay

VARIABLES epoch, inService, holder, holdEpoch, drawing

vars == <<epoch, inService, holder, holdEpoch, drawing>>

TypeOK ==
    /\ epoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ inService \subseteq Bays
    /\ holder \in Bays \cup {NoBay}
    /\ holdEpoch \in 0 .. MaxEpoch
    /\ drawing \subseteq Bays

Init ==
    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ inService = Bays
    /\ holder = NoBay
    /\ holdEpoch = 0
    /\ drawing = {}

\* The high-pressure manifold is granted to one bay at a time, and the grant
\* records the line epoch it was made under.
Grant(b) ==
    /\ holder = NoBay
    /\ b \in inService
    /\ holder' = b
    /\ holdEpoch' = epoch
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inService, drawing>>

\* Water only comes on for a grant made under the epoch the line is running.
Open(b) ==
    /\ holder = b
    /\ holdEpoch = epoch
    /\ b \in inService
    /\ drawing = {}
    /\ drawing' = {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inService, holder, holdEpoch>>

Close(b) ==
    /\ b \in drawing
    /\ drawing' = drawing \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inService, holder, holdEpoch>>

Release(b) ==
    /\ holder = b
    /\ drawing = {}
    /\ holder' = NoBay
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inService, holdEpoch, drawing>>

Reaffirm(b) ==
    /\ holder = b
    /\ holdEpoch # epoch
    /\ b \in inService
    /\ holdEpoch' = epoch
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, inService, holder, drawing>>

\* Reconfiguration renumbers the line: bays are taken out of or put back into
\* service, the water is shut off, and any grant made earlier is now behind.
Reconfigure(a) ==
    /\ a # {}
    /\ inService' = a
    /\ epoch' = IF epoch = MaxEpoch THEN 0 ELSE epoch + 1
    /\ drawing' = {}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, holdEpoch>>

Releasing == \E b \in Bays : Release(b)
Closing == \E b \in Bays : Close(b)

Next ==
    \/ \E b \in Bays : Grant(b) \/ Open(b) \/ Close(b) \/ Release(b) \/ Reaffirm(b)
    \/ \E a \in SUBSET Bays : Reconfigure(a)

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ SF_vars(Releasing) /\ WF_vars(Closing)

\* Whichever bay has water is the bay currently holding the manifold, under a
\* grant made in the epoch the line is running and on a bay still in service.
ManifoldExclusive ==
    \A b \in drawing :
        /\ holder = b
        /\ holdEpoch = epoch
        /\ b \in inService

\* The manifold never stays in one bay's hands: every grant is given back.
GrantsGiveBack == (holder # NoBay) ~> (holder = NoBay)

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Bays = {byPrewash, byFoam, byRinse}
    MaxEpoch = 2
    NoBay = NoBay
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT ManifoldExclusive
PROPERTY GrantsGiveBack
nl:
A car-wash conveyor line runs cars past a row of treatment bays that all draw from one
high-pressure water manifold. The manifold can supply one bay at a time: two bays drawing at once
drops the pressure below what either needs and leaves cars half-washed, so use of the manifold is
exclusive.

The line is numbered by epoch. A bay is granted the manifold only while it is in service, and the
grant records the epoch the line was running when it was made. Water only comes on for a grant made
under the epoch the line is currently running: a grant from an earlier epoch describes a line layout
that no longer exists, and the valves stay shut for it. A bay whose grant is behind can reaffirm it
against the running epoch, provided it is still in service, and then draw as normal. Water is shut
off again when the bay is done, and the manifold is given back once the water is off. The manifold
never stays in one bay's hands for ever.

Capacity changes while the line runs. Reconfiguration puts bays into or out of service — the site
adds a wax stage in summer, drops the pre-wash when the tanker is late — and always leaves at least
one bay in service. Reconfiguring renumbers the line to the next epoch, wrapping at the top of the
range, and shuts the water off in the same movement, so nothing is drawing across a layout change
and every grant made before it is now behind.

The full set of actions is: Grant, in which the free manifold is granted to an in-service bay and
the grant is stamped with the running epoch; Open, in which water comes on for a bay holding a
current grant on an in-service bay, while nothing else is drawing; Close, in which a drawing bay
shuts its water off; Release, in which a bay with the water off gives the manifold back; Reaffirm,
in which a bay holding a grant from an earlier epoch brings it up to the running epoch; and
Reconfigure, in which the set of in-service bays is changed, the line epoch rolls on and the water
is shut off.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Any bay drawing water is the one bay currently holding the manifold, under a grant
stamped with the epoch the line is running, on a bay that is still in service.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: The manifold is never held for ever — every grant is eventually given back.

---- MODULE W4Od7m6p3t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cranes, Cells, Horizon, MaxHold, Bare

VARIABLES leases, clock, seen, landed

vars == <<leases, clock, seen, landed>>

Bookings == [cell: Cells, crane: Cranes, until: 1 .. Horizon]

Held(c) == \E l \in leases : l.crane = c
LiveOn(k) == \E l \in leases : l.cell = k /\ l.until > clock

TypeOK ==
    /\ leases \subseteq Bookings
    /\ clock \in 0 .. Horizon
    /\ seen \in [Cranes -> 0 .. Horizon]
    /\ landed \in [Cells -> Cranes \cup {Bare}]

Init ==
    /\ leases = {}
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ seen = [c \in Cranes |-> 0]
    /\ landed = [k \in Cells |-> Bare]

\* A crane whose clock reading has fallen behind is slow, not broken: the yard
\* office simply refuses to book against a stale reading.
Book(c, k, len) ==
    /\ seen[c] = clock
    /\ ~Held(c)
    /\ ~LiveOn(k)
    /\ clock + len <= Horizon
    /\ leases' = leases \cup {[cell |-> k, crane |-> c, until |-> clock + len]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, seen, landed>>

Refresh(c) ==
    /\ seen[c] # clock
    /\ seen' = [seen EXCEPT ![c] = clock]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leases, clock, landed>>

Land(c, k) ==
    /\ seen[c] = clock
    /\ landed[k] = Bare
    /\ \E l \in leases : l.cell = k /\ l.crane = c /\ l.until > clock
    /\ landed' = [landed EXCEPT ![k] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leases, clock, seen>>

Lift(c, k) ==
    /\ landed[k] = c
    /\ landed' = [landed EXCEPT ![k] = Bare]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leases, clock, seen>>

\* Time moves whether or not the cranes are keeping up; readings that were
\* current a moment ago are now behind.
Tick ==
    /\ clock < Horizon
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leases, seen, landed>>

Purge(l) ==
    /\ l \in leases
    /\ l.until <= clock
    /\ leases' = leases \ {l}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, seen, landed>>

Handover ==
    /\ leases = {}
    /\ \A k \in Cells : landed[k] = Bare
    /\ clock' = 0
    /\ seen' = [c \in Cranes |-> 0]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leases, landed>>

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cranes, k \in Cells, n \in 1 .. MaxHold : Book(c, k, n)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Refresh(c)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes, k \in Cells : Land(c, k) \/ Lift(c, k)
    \/ \E l \in leases : Purge(l)
    \/ Tick \/ Handover

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* No stack cell is ever under two bookings that are both still running, so a
\* cell is never allocated to two cranes at the same time.
NoDoubleBooking ==
    \A a, b \in leases :
        (a # b /\ a.cell = b.cell) => (a.until <= clock \/ b.until <= clock)

====

CONSTANTS
    Cranes = {crQuay, crYard}
    Cells = {clRowA, clRowB}
    Horizon = 3
    MaxHold = 2
    Bare = Bare
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT NoDoubleBooking
nl:
A container terminal stacks boxes into numbered cells in the yard. A cell takes one box at a time, so
the yard office must never have two cranes booked onto the same cell at once — two cranes swinging
for one stack cell is a wrecked box at best.

Cells are booked on leases with an expiry. A crane books a cell for a chosen number of minutes,
and the office grants it only if that cell is not already under a booking that is still running, the
crane is not already holding a booking of its own, and the expiry falls inside the shift. A booking
that has run out is purged and the cell goes back into the pool.

The cranes are slow, not broken. Each crane works from the clock reading it last took, and time
moves on whether or not the crane has kept up, so a crane can be sitting on a reading that is minutes
behind the yard. The office refuses to deal with a crane whose reading is behind: it will not book a
cell on a stale reading and it will not accept a landing on one. A crane that notices it has fallen
behind refreshes its reading and carries on. Nothing here is a failure — the slow crane always
catches up eventually, it just cannot act in the meantime.

A crane lands a box into a cell only against a booking of its own that is still running, with a
current clock reading and the cell empty. Boxes are lifted back out in the ordinary course of
working the ship. At the shift handover, with no bookings outstanding and the yard clear, the clock
and every crane's reading are reset.

The full set of actions is: Book, in which a crane with a current reading and no booking of its own
takes a cell that is not already under a running booking, for a period inside the shift; Refresh, in
which a crane brings its clock reading up to date; Land, in which a crane with a current reading puts
a box into an empty cell it holds a running booking on; Lift, in which a box is taken back out of a
cell; Tick, in which the yard clock advances a minute; Purge, in which a booking that has run out is
cleared away; and Handover, in which the clock and every crane's reading are reset once no bookings
are outstanding and the yard is clear.

SAFETY PROPERTY: No stack cell is ever under two bookings that are both still running, so a cell is
never allocated to two cranes at the same time.

---- MODULE W4Od10m6p4t4 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Trains, Sections, Horizon, MaxDraw, MaxFeed

VARIABLES grants, clock, feed, drawing

vars == <<grants, clock, feed, drawing>>

Grants == [sec: Sections, train: Trains, amps: 1 .. MaxDraw, until: 1 .. Horizon]

RECURSIVE Amps(_)
Amps(S) ==
    IF S = {} THEN 0
    ELSE LET g == CHOOSE x \in S : TRUE IN g.amps + Amps(S \ {g})

Running(s) == {g \in grants : g.sec = s /\ g.until > clock}
LoadOn(s) == Amps(Running(s))
Booked(t) == \E g \in grants : g.train = t

TypeOK ==
    /\ grants \subseteq Grants
    /\ clock \in 0 .. Horizon
    /\ feed \in [Sections -> 1 .. MaxFeed]
    /\ drawing \subseteq Trains

Init ==
    /\ grants = {}
    /\ clock = 0
    /\ feed = [s \in Sections |-> MaxFeed]
    /\ drawing = {}

\* Traction allowance is let on a lease with an expiry, and the allowance
\* counts against the substation from the moment it is let.
Allow(t, s, a, len) ==
    /\ ~Booked(t)
    /\ clock + len <= Horizon
    /\ LoadOn(s) + a <= feed[s]
    /\ grants' = grants \cup {[sec |-> s, train |-> t, amps |-> a, until |-> clock + len]}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, feed, drawing>>

Notch(t) ==
    /\ t \notin drawing
    /\ \E g \in grants : g.train = t /\ g.until > clock
    /\ drawing' = drawing \cup {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<grants, clock, feed>>

Coast(t) ==
    /\ t \in drawing
    /\ drawing' = drawing \ {t}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<grants, clock, feed>>

Tick ==
    /\ clock < Horizon
    /\ clock' = clock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<grants, feed, drawing>>

\* A lapsed allowance is torn up and the train it belonged to comes off power
\* in the same movement.
Lapse(g) ==
    /\ g \in grants
    /\ g.until <= clock
    /\ grants' = grants \ {g}
    /\ drawing' = drawing \ {g.train}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<clock, feed>>

\* The substation is rerated while the railway runs, but never below what its
\* section has already been promised.
Rerate(s, c) ==
    /\ c >= LoadOn(s)
    /\ feed' = [feed EXCEPT ![s] = c]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<grants, clock, drawing>>

NewDay ==
    /\ grants = {}
    /\ clock = Horizon
    /\ clock' = 0
    /\ UNCHANGED <<grants, feed, drawing>>

Ticking == Tick
Lapsing == \E g \in grants : Lapse(g)

Next ==
    \/ \E t \in Trains, s \in Sections, a \in 1 .. MaxDraw, n \in 1 .. Horizon :
           Allow(t, s, a, n)
    \/ \E t \in Trains : Notch(t) \/ Coast(t)
    \/ \E s \in Sections, c \in 1 .. MaxFeed : Rerate(s, c)
    \/ Ticking \/ Lapsing \/ NewDay

Spec ==
    /\ Init /\ [][Next]_vars
    /\ WF_vars(Ticking) /\ WF_vars(Lapsing)

\* The traction allowances still running on a section never add up to more than
\* what that section's substation can feed.
FeedNeverOversubscribed ==
    \A s \in Sections : LoadOn(s) <= feed[s]

\* Allowances are never held for ever: the register always empties out.
AllowancesLapse == (grants # {}) ~> (grants = {})

====

CONSTANTS
    Trains = {tnUp, tnDown}
    Sections = {secRiver, secDepot}
    Horizon = 3
    MaxDraw = 2
    MaxFeed = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT FeedNeverOversubscribed
PROPERTY AllowancesLapse
nl:
A subway line feeds traction current to its track sections from substations, and each substation can
supply only so many amps at once. Drawing more than a section's substation can feed trips the
breaker and leaves trains stranded between stations, so the allowance handed out on a section must
never add up to more than the substation can deliver.

Allowances are let on leases with an expiry rather than handed over for the day. A train is granted
an allowance on a section for a chosen number of amps and a chosen number of minutes, and the office
grants it only if the train is not already holding an allowance, the expiry falls inside the
operating day, and what is already promised on that section leaves room for it. The promise counts
against the substation from the moment it is made, not from the moment the train actually notches
up.

A train notches up onto power only against an allowance of its own that is still running, and coasts
back off power in the ordinary course of driving. When an allowance lapses it is torn up and the
train it belonged to comes off power in the same movement, so nothing is ever drawing on an expired
promise. Allowances are never held indefinitely: the register always empties out.

Substation capacity changes while the railway runs — a transformer is taken out for maintenance, a
second feeder is switched in — but a section is never rerated below what it has already promised to
the trains running on it. At the end of the operating day, once no allowances are outstanding, the
clock is reset.

The full set of actions is: Allow, in which a train holding no allowance is granted amps on a
section for a period inside the day, provided the section has room; Notch, in which a train with a
running allowance comes onto power; Coast, in which a train comes off power; Tick, in which the
clock advances a minute; Lapse, in which an expired allowance is torn up and its train comes off
power; Rerate, in which a substation's capacity is changed at runtime, never below what its section
has already promised; and NewDay, in which the clock is reset once no allowances are outstanding.

SAFETY PROPERTY: On every section, the traction allowances that are still running never add up to
more than that section's substation can feed.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Allowances are never held for ever — the allowance register always eventually
empties out.

---- MODULE W4Od5m4p2t0 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences, FiniteSets

CONSTANTS Workers, Roles, Roster, QCap

VARIABLES lounge, queue, hand, playing, alive

vars == <<lounge, queue, hand, playing, alive>>

Carried == Cardinality({w \in Workers : hand[w] = 1})

TypeOK ==
    /\ lounge \in 0 .. Roster
    /\ Len(queue) <= QCap
    /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(queue) : queue[i] \in Roles
    /\ hand \in [Workers -> 0 .. 1]
    /\ playing \in 0 .. Roster
    /\ alive \subseteq Workers

Init ==
    /\ lounge = Roster
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ hand = [w \in Workers |-> 0]
    /\ playing = 0
    /\ alive = Workers

\* Backpressure: a player in the lounge cannot join once the queue is full.
Join(r) ==
    /\ lounge > 0
    /\ Len(queue) < QCap
    /\ lounge' = lounge - 1
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, r)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<hand, playing, alive>>

Pull(w) ==
    /\ w \in alive
    /\ hand[w] = 0
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ hand' = [hand EXCEPT ![w] = 1]
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lounge, playing, alive>>

Seat(w) ==
    /\ w \in alive
    /\ hand[w] = 1
    /\ hand' = [hand EXCEPT ![w] = 0]
    /\ playing' = playing + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lounge, queue, alive>>

Requeue(w, r) ==
    /\ w \in alive
    /\ hand[w] = 1
    /\ Len(queue) < QCap
    /\ hand' = [hand EXCEPT ![w] = 0]
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, r)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lounge, playing, alive>>

Finish ==
    /\ playing > 0
    /\ playing' = playing - 1
    /\ lounge' = lounge + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, hand, alive>>

\* A matchmaking worker can die without a word, still holding the player it
\* pulled; that player is neither queued nor seated until the sweep runs.
Die(w) ==
    /\ w \in alive
    /\ alive' = alive \ {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lounge, queue, hand, playing>>

Sweep(w) ==
    /\ w \notin alive
    /\ hand[w] = 1
    /\ hand' = [hand EXCEPT ![w] = 0]
    /\ lounge' = lounge + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<queue, playing, alive>>

Respawn(w) ==
    /\ w \notin alive
    /\ hand[w] = 0
    /\ alive' = alive \cup {w}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<lounge, queue, hand, playing>>

Next ==
    \/ \E r \in Roles : Join(r)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Pull(w) \/ Seat(w) \/ Die(w) \/ Sweep(w) \/ Respawn(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers, r \in Roles : Requeue(w, r)
    \/ Finish

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Every player on the roster is in exactly one place -- the lounge, the queue,
\* a worker's hand, or a live match -- so the four counts always add to the
\* roster, even across a worker dying mid-pull.
PlayersConserved ==
    lounge + Len(queue) + Carried + playing = Roster

====
cfg_text:
CONSTANTS
    Workers = {wkAlpha, wkBeta}
    Roles = {roTank, roHealer}
    Roster = 3
    QCap = 2
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT PlayersConserved
nl:
A multiplayer game lobby matchmaker takes players from the lounge, queues them up, and seats them
into matches. The roster is fixed: every player on it is in exactly one place at any instant — idle
in the lounge, waiting in the queue, held in a matchmaking worker's hand, or in a live match — and
the matchmaker must never lose a player or conjure one up out of nowhere.

The queue is bounded and applies backpressure. A player in the lounge can join the queue only while
there is room in it; once the queue is at its cap, joining is refused and the player waits in the
lounge instead. Matchmaking workers pull from the head of the queue one player at a time, and a
worker holds at most one player. A held player is either seated into a live match or put back onto
the tail of the queue, and putting back is itself subject to the cap. Matches end and the players in
them return to the lounge.

A matchmaking worker can die without a word — no error, no handback — while still holding the
player it pulled. That player is in nobody's queue and in no match: it sits in the dead worker's
hand until the sweep runs, and the sweep is what puts it back into the lounge. A worker holding
nothing can be respawned and start pulling again.

The full set of actions is: Join, in which a player leaves the lounge for the tail of the queue while
the queue is below its cap; Pull, in which a live worker holding nothing takes the player at the head
of the queue into its hand; Seat, in which a live worker puts the player it holds into a live match;
Requeue, in which a live worker puts the player it holds back onto the tail of the queue, if there
is room; Finish, in which a match ends and its player returns to the lounge; Die, in which a worker
stops without warning while still holding a player; Sweep, in which the player held by a dead worker
is returned to the lounge; and Respawn, in which a dead worker holding nothing is brought back.

SAFETY PROPERTY: The players idle in the lounge, waiting in the queue, held in workers' hands and in
live matches always add up to exactly the roster.

---- MODULE W4Od7m0p3t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals

CONSTANTS Cranes, Cells, MaxVer, Free, NoCell, NoReq

VARIABLES ver, booking, assigned, held, pending

vars == <<ver, booking, assigned, held, pending>>

Reqs == [crane: Cranes, cell: Cells, saw: 0 .. MaxVer]

Roll(v) == IF v = MaxVer THEN 0 ELSE v + 1

TypeOK ==
    /\ ver \in [Cells -> 0 .. MaxVer]
    /\ booking \in [Cells -> Cranes \cup {Free}]
    /\ assigned \in [Cranes -> Cells \cup {NoCell}]
    /\ held \in [Cranes -> 0 .. MaxVer]
    /\ pending \in Reqs \cup {NoReq}

Init ==
    /\ ver = [k \in Cells |-> 0]
    /\ booking = [k \in Cells |-> Free]
    /\ assigned = [c \in Cranes |-> NoCell]
    /\ held = [c \in Cranes |-> 0]
    /\ pending = NoReq

\* The crane reads the cell's survey number and lodges a request; it does not
\* hold anything while the office works through it.
Submit(c, k) ==
    /\ pending = NoReq
    /\ assigned[c] = NoCell
    /\ pending' = [crane |-> c, cell |-> k, saw |-> ver[k]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, booking, assigned, held>>

\* The request is honoured only if the survey number has not moved since the
\* crane read it and the cell is still unbooked.
Commit ==
    /\ pending # NoReq
    /\ ver[pending.cell] = pending.saw
    /\ booking[pending.cell] = Free
    /\ booking' = [booking EXCEPT ![pending.cell] = pending.crane]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![pending.cell] = Roll(@)]
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![pending.crane] = pending.cell]
    /\ held' = [held EXCEPT ![pending.crane] = Roll(ver[pending.cell])]
    /\ pending' = NoReq

Reject ==
    /\ pending # NoReq
    /\ \/ ver[pending.cell] # pending.saw
       \/ booking[pending.cell] # Free
    /\ pending' = NoReq
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ver, booking, assigned, held>>

\* Re-surveying an unbooked cell moves its number on, which is exactly what
\* leaves a slow crane's request standing on a reading that has gone stale.
Resurvey(k) ==
    /\ booking[k] = Free
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![k] = Roll(@)]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<booking, assigned, held, pending>>

Vacate(c) ==
    /\ assigned[c] # NoCell
    /\ booking' = [booking EXCEPT ![assigned[c]] = Free]
    /\ ver' = [ver EXCEPT ![assigned[c]] = Roll(@)]
    /\ assigned' = [assigned EXCEPT ![c] = NoCell]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<held, pending>>

Resolving == Commit \/ Reject

Next ==
    \/ \E c \in Cranes, k \in Cells : Submit(c, k)
    \/ Resolving
    \/ \E k \in Cells : Resurvey(k)
    \/ \E c \in Cranes : Vacate(c)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars /\ WF_vars(Resolving)

\* Every crane that has been given a cell is recorded as that cell's booking
\* and holds the survey number the cell currently carries, so no cell is ever
\* allocated to two cranes at once.
AssignmentMatchesBooking ==
    \A c \in Cranes :
        assigned[c] # NoCell =>
            /\ booking[assigned[c]] = c
            /\ ver[assigned[c]] = held[c]

\* The office never sits on a request: every one lodged is eventually settled.
RequestsSettle == (pending # NoReq) ~> (pending = NoReq)

CONSTANTS
    Cranes = {crShip, crRail}
    Cells = {clBayOne, clBayTwo}
    MaxVer = 1
    Free = Free
    NoCell = NoCell
    NoReq = NoReq
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT AssignmentMatchesBooking
PROPERTY RequestsSettle
nl:
A container terminal allocates yard cells to its cranes. A cell takes one crane's work at a time, so
the yard office must never allocate the same cell to two cranes.

Nothing is locked up front. A crane reads the survey number the office is showing for a cell, then
lodges a request naming the cell and the number it read. It does not hold the cell while the request
sits in the office. The office honours the request only if the survey number has not moved since the
crane read it and the cell is still unbooked; when it does, the cell is booked to that crane, the
survey number moves on, and the crane is given the new number to keep. If the number has moved, or
the cell was booked in the meantime, the request is turned down and the crane starts again. Survey
numbers are small wrapping counters that roll back to zero at the top. Only one request sits in the
office at a time, and the office never sits on one: every request lodged is eventually either
honoured or turned down.

The cranes are slow, not broken. A crane can take a long time between reading a number and lodging
its request, and the yard does not wait: the office re-surveys unbooked cells as stacks are
rearranged, which moves their numbers on and leaves a slow crane's request standing on a reading
that has gone stale. That is not a failure and needs no recovery — the request is simply turned down
and the crane reads again.

A crane vacates the cell it was given when it has finished with it, which unbooks the cell and moves
its survey number on again.

The full set of actions is: Submit, in which a crane with no cell of its own reads a cell's survey
number and lodges a request, provided the office is free; Commit, in which the office honours a
request whose number is unmoved and whose cell is unbooked, booking the cell, moving the number on
and giving the new number to the crane; Reject, in which the office turns a request down because the
number moved or the cell was taken; Resurvey, in which an unbooked cell's survey number is moved on
as the yard is rearranged; and Vacate, in which a crane gives up the cell it holds, unbooking it and
moving its number on.

SAFETY PROPERTY: Every crane that has been given a cell is recorded as that cell's booking and holds
the survey number that cell currently carries, so a cell is never allocated to two cranes at once.

LIVENESS PROPERTY: Every request lodged with the yard office is eventually settled, one way or the
other.

---- MODULE W4Od2m4p5t3 ----
EXTENDS Naturals, Sequences

CONSTANTS Bots, Pallets, QCap, NoPallet

VARIABLES belt, carrying, banded, lagging

vars == <<belt, carrying, banded, lagging>>

OnBelt(p) == \E i \in 1 .. Len(belt) : belt[i] = p
InHand(p) == \E b \in Bots : carrying[b] = p

TypeOK ==
    /\ Len(belt) <= QCap
    /\ \A i \in 1 .. Len(belt) : belt[i] \in Pallets
    /\ carrying \in [Bots -> Pallets \cup {NoPallet}]
    /\ banded \subseteq Pallets
    /\ lagging \subseteq Bots

Init ==
    /\ belt = <<>>
    /\ carrying = [b \in Bots |-> NoPallet]
    /\ banded = {}
    /\ lagging = {}

\* Backpressure: nothing joins the belt once it is at its cap, and a pallet
\* already banded, queued or in a gripper is never queued again.
Queue(p) ==
    /\ Len(belt) < QCap
    /\ p \notin banded
    /\ ~OnBelt(p)
    /\ ~InHand(p)
    /\ belt' = Append(belt, p)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<carrying, banded, lagging>>

Take(b) ==
    /\ carrying[b] = NoPallet
    /\ belt # <<>>
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![b] = Head(belt)]
    /\ belt' = Tail(belt)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<banded, lagging>>

\* Banding a pallet cuts and welds the strap: there is no way back from it, so
\* it must happen to a pallet once and once only.
Band(b) ==
    /\ b \notin lagging
    /\ carrying[b] # NoPallet
    /\ banded' = banded \cup {carrying[b]}
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![b] = NoPallet]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<belt, lagging>>

Replace(b) ==
    /\ carrying[b] # NoPallet
    /\ Len(belt) < QCap
    /\ belt' = Append(belt, carrying[b])
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![b] = NoPallet]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<banded, lagging>>

\* A bot can fall behind without failing: it still has the pallet in its
\* gripper, it just is not going to band it any time soon.
Lag(b) ==
    /\ b \notin lagging
    /\ lagging' = lagging \cup {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<belt, carrying, banded>>

CatchUp(b) ==
    /\ b \in lagging
    /\ lagging' = lagging \ {b}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<belt, carrying, banded>>

\* The floor supervisor takes a pallet back off a lagging bot rather than wait
\* for it; the bot is left holding nothing, so it cannot band it later.
Recall(b) ==
    /\ b \in lagging
    /\ carrying[b] # NoPallet
    /\ Len(belt) < QCap
    /\ belt' = Append(belt, carrying[b])
    /\ carrying' = [carrying EXCEPT ![b] = NoPallet]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<banded, lagging>>

Next ==
    \/ \E p \in Pallets : Queue(p)
    \/ \E b \in Bots : Take(b) \/ Band(b) \/ Replace(b) \/ Lag(b) \/ CatchUp(b) \/ Recall(b)

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

\* Once a pallet has been banded it is nowhere else in the system -- not on the
\* belt, not in any gripper -- so nothing can present it for banding again.
BandedPalletsAreGone ==
    \A p \in banded : ~OnBelt(p) /\ ~InHand(p)

CONSTANTS
    Bots = {btOne, btTwo}
    Pallets = {plA, plB, plC}
    QCap = 2
    NoPallet = NoPallet
SPECIFICATION Spec
INVARIANT BandedPalletsAreGone
nl:
A warehouse robot fleet feeds pallets to a strapping station. Banding a pallet cuts the strap to
length and welds it: there is no way back from it, and a pallet that goes through twice comes out
with two straps crossed over each other and has to be broken down by hand. So a pallet must be
banded once and once only.

Work reaches the bots on a bounded belt with backpressure. A pallet joins the tail of the belt only
while the belt is below its cap, and only if it is not already banded, not already somewhere on the
belt, and not already sitting in a bot's gripper — so the belt never carries the same pallet twice
and never carries one that is already done. Bots take pallets off the head of the belt one at a
time, and a bot holds at most one pallet. A bot can put its pallet back on the tail of the belt
instead of banding it, again subject to the cap.

A bot can fall behind without failing. A lagging bot still has its pallet in the gripper and is
perfectly healthy — it is simply not going to get to the strapping head any time soon, and it will
not band anything while it is behind. It catches up on its own eventually. Rather than wait, the
floor supervisor can recall the pallet from a lagging bot and put it back on the belt; the bot is
then holding nothing, so when it does catch up there is nothing for it to band.

The full set of actions is: Queue, in which a pallet that is not banded, not on the belt and not in
a gripper joins the tail of the belt while the belt is below its cap; Take, in which a bot holding
nothing lifts the pallet at the head of the belt; Band, in which a bot that is not lagging straps
the pallet it holds and lets it go; Replace, in which a bot puts the pallet it holds back on the
tail of the belt; Lag, in which a bot falls behind while still holding its pallet; CatchUp, in which
a lagging bot comes back up to speed; and Recall, in which the supervisor takes the pallet off a
lagging bot and puts it back on the belt.

SAFETY PROPERTY: A pallet that has been banded is nowhere else in the system — not anywhere on the
belt and not in any bot's gripper — so it can never be presented for banding a second time.
